## Part F. Numbered maintainer decisions

The following are proposed questions, not rulings. Each item record names exactly one decision; D01 additionally gates every0.9 adoption. Recommendations retain all capabilities even if mechanics are staged.

**D01. Approve separate compatible 0.2.11/ISA 0.8 and capability 0.3/ISA 0.9 tracks, with publication and execution gates rather than immediate retargeting?**

Recommendation: Yes. Preserve accepted bytes; gate 0.3 on published ISA 0.9, muse disposition, maintainer K64/K65 ratification, published reference-library binding and independent ISA 0.9 execution. K64/K65 define non-row support and whole-cleanup ordinals (ISA-11-P10, ISA-11-P11), relevant to all scheduled/certificate realisations, not new LLVM capability exclusions.

**D02. Retain the staged per-region table and all four budget units, with no new table ABI?**

Recommendation: Yes; I05/I33 retain canonical identity selection, counters and sstack accounting.

**D03. Retain the version2 descriptor with independent ARG/IN/MEM_IN/OUT bindings and existing common-delivery scheme?**

Recommendation: Yes; I06/I17, including zero-output execution and 2k-1 wide delivery.

**D04. Retain the full lifted closure and all seven own-format FP implementations?**

Recommendation: Yes; I07/I15 keep the complete generic-intrinsic inventory, vector/limb order and native-materialised differential contract.

**D05. Retain the four per-tier device models and libc/VFS shims as ordinary bitcode?**

Recommendation: Yes; I13, with R terminal faults updated by D18 and no silent host execution in R/L.

**D06. Retain polyvariant clones, one A(F), shared globals and bounded-program compare-tree dispatch?**

Recommendation: Yes; I22/I35/I23/I30. No new indirect-call ISA opcode is required.

**D07. Retain the exact field/interval-sensitive reference analysis and general allocator/call-return propagation?**

Recommendation: Yes; I11/I24/I26/I27/I28, with no reliance on discarded range metadata or declared array size as an index bound.

**D08. Retain Cl/M/Co TDL and direct-body handling of reversible markers during action generation?**

Recommendation: Yes; I01/I31, including clean control workspace and accepted overwrite/inverse obligations.

**D09. Retain requested deferred measurement and the accepted benign-attribute lists?**

Recommendation: Yes; I08/I21, with channel-boundary and LLVM-legality evidence kept distinct.

**D10. Retain runtime op/class dispatch over the complete valid tables?**

Recommendation: Yes; I04/I18. Out-of-table cases retain their existing precise diagnostics.

**D11. Retain clean fallback for CC-spanning borrowing and allocation-generation handle equality?**

Recommendation: Yes; I09/I10. Direct dirty borrowing outside actions remains optional efficiency, not an extra blocker.

**D12. Retain EH/sjlj/fibers, target asm classification, varargs and the complete riscv64 platform?**

Recommendation: Yes; I12/I36/I37/I39. Continue platform inventory and actual boot/oracle gates; no unsupported-subset shortcut.

**D13. Retain tested mixed-major linkage and closed-unit mode with whole-program fallback?**

Recommendation: Yes; I16/I34. Actual link execution remains required evidence.

**D14. Choose native K4 only for covering exhaustive/library claims, while retaining CC expansion for the existing sampled/assumed inverse path?**

Recommendation: Choose that dual construction; I03/I14. Do not reinterpret sampled evidence or T-CLEAN as a native K4 proof.

**D15. Adopt dynamic classical qreg widths and coherent padding to a sound materialised/type-domain bound?**

Recommendation: Yes; I19. Keep n>=1 and transfer checks. Full unsigned i64-domain padding is the conservative fallback when AV top supplies no smaller bound; cost can be enormous but the analysis cap is not a scope cap.

**D16. Adopt exact device budget.mint with tuple-bound schedules and reversible token validity?**

Recommendation: Yes; I20. Preserve existing host/static paths and forbid tuple rounding.

**D17. Adopt persistent lossless tag-to-ledger-id lookup across entries, with exclusive run ownership?**

Recommendation: Yes; I25/I29/I-cbe. Keep pointer-width tags and an explicit bijection/bridge rather than assuming every pointer can store an ISA64 id; remove static-file bounds only on the0.9 target.

**D18. Adopt K2/K5/K6 R ledger operations, typed terminal faults and eligible failed-run reversal?**

Recommendation: Yes; I02/I32/I38/I-bz6. R faults terminate the whole run, not return status to a continuing CC caller; budget enforcement stays dialect instrumentation.

**D19. Retain runtime entry replay and extend its snapshot preparation/release to R using K2?**

Recommendation: Yes; I40. No overlay primitive or build-time-only restriction; charge replay and preserve allocator identity.

**D20. Treat 0t9 as an already-applied example correction, pending regression evidence rather than another spec change?**

Recommendation: Yes; I-0t9. Keep candidates=classical in the inherited example and test first-operand order.

**D21. Clarify PT12 using the complete virtual N9 value transfer in the compatible track?**

Recommendation: Yes; I-0y2. Execute xor and both cmpxchg paths; preserve its nonblocking status relative to accepted 0.2.10.

**D22. Adopt ISA 0.9 invocation/claim binding while retaining metadata fallbacks and honest fixed-region evidence labels?**

Recommendation: Yes; I-gwf. No schema invention and no claim of full-D proof for a strict fixed-image subdomain; rung4 verification remains complete on its declared fixed-database space.

## ISA proposal disposition

**New ISA beads filed: none.** K1/K2/K3/K5/K6 contain the actual missing0.8 capability sentences. K4 is optional and does not replace the sampled CC construction. G-12/13/14/15/16, direct CC dirty borrowing and native indirect calls retain explicit constructions; they are efficiency work, not newly discovered ISA blockers. Exact sentences formerly needed for bz6/cbe are cited in those records. Fixed-region proof labelling and dedicated certificate metadata fields remain wording/schema questions in the already-open gwf bead, with capability-preserving metadata/evidence defaults. K64/K65 need ratification, not duplicate proposal beads.

### PT12 spelling hardening — 2026-10-31

A final boundary probe exposed a remaining PT12 parser bug: with explicit
`ptr addrspace(1)` the address string included the type suffix and lost its
tracked object, so neither xor nor cmpxchg added 3 to the memory domain.
Both subtests failed (`scripts/.tmp/0211-atomic-spelling-red.txt`). The shared
N9 grammar parser now separates pointer type/value, strips weak/volatile and
ordering/syncscope syntax, preserves alignment and emits the original typed
pointer in virtual/materialised loads and stores. Pointer-valued atomic
storage widths use P(a). No semantic exclusion or new ISA requirement.

New checked rows `pt12-xor-as1` and `pt12-cmpxchg-as1` exercise the spelling
end to end: LLVM18/23 verify and native materialised O0/O3 give the same
old/success/width/clean-free/code tuples as their unqualified companions.
0y2 was reopened during this hardening and closed again after the final
**2834/2834** green gate (`scripts/.tmp/0211-freeze.json`), 92 checker tests
and 7 legacy runtime tests. The 115-file source manifest stayed unchanged.
No additional normative sentence is introduced: the PT12 clarification applies
to all admitted LLVM atomic spellings already. The full manifest now binds
five PT12 native states, not only the original three.

Rejected alternatives by item (from the ruled outline; none adopted):

- **I01**: Generation-only execution changes the controlled store result; retaining incidental garbage as undeclared outputs violates the accepted cleanup contract.
- **I03**: Reinstating BLK-3 is false; replacing every pair with native qinplace would exclude the sampled path described in I14.
- **I04**: Accepting only class zero or merging classes without names loses the requested resource class.
- **I05**: Iterating the final hash back into lookup creates cycles; steps-only records or source edits would restore the narrowing.
- **I06**: Packing all inputs or constant-specialising every runtime argument imposes source/ABI restrictions the accepted descriptor removed.
- **I07**: A scalar-only profile, silently trapping an unsupported generic intrinsic, or limiting the contract to checker seeds narrows scope.
- **I08**: Measuring immediately changes the controlled instrument; uncopying retained channel records silently turns the channel into a unitary.
- **I09**: Reinstating T-BORROW drops capability; treating arbitrary dirty state as clean without restoration is unsound.
- **I10**: Physical-slot equality or id truncation aliases generations; banning null checks again breaks unmodified language idioms.
- **I11**: A new whitelist of wrapper names or TOP for every non-libc return reinstates the same restriction; inventing freshness for opaque external code is unsound.
- **I12**: Rejecting all unwinding or replacing an in-region catch with fault 4 changes defined program behaviour.
- **I13**: F(8) for a modelled VFS/entropy call narrows SQLite/Monte Carlo; native host calls from R/L violate effect closure.
- **I14**: Library-only admission narrows scope; claiming a sampled maximum is B_min or using a sampled claim as K4 authority is unsound.
- **I15**: Silent widening through f64/native long double, deleting retained fneg/transport, or faulting uncovered checker formats would narrow the accepted contract.
- **I16**: One-major-only linkage or promising arbitrary newer bitcode beyond the tested reader both contradict the envelope contract.
- **I17**: Source packing wrappers, return-only results, the superseded k+2 scheme or deleting the zero-output call change the admitted interface or fault outcome.
- **I18**: BD-E-OPERAND-UNBOUNDED for a finite-table selector reinstates the narrowing; remapping an invalid code silently is incorrect.
- **I21**: Reverting to the spike-only whitelist narrows build flags; declaring all attributes benign permits elimination/speculation.
- **I22**: Duplicating globals changes state; replacing stored addresses by clone addresses breaks comparisons/VFS tables; restoring BD-E-DEVICE-ADDRESS narrows libraries.
- **I23**: Blanket address-taken/indirect escape rejects visible device code; allowing an opaque host callee to consume handles violates containment.
- **I24**: Constant-lane-only acceptance narrows collections; merging packed scalar integers as lane values or dropping ROOTs is unsound.
- **I26**: Object-level escape bans prohibit lists/trees; ignoring an actual unknown reader discards the north-star containment rule.
- **I27**: Field-insensitive TOP restores the false rejection; assuming array bounds or using mathematical instead of modular GEP loses reachable slots.
- **I28**: A name-based host-reference ban confuses unrelated fields; letting host native code dereference or perform arithmetic on handles violates provenance.
- **I30**: Rejecting every imprecise candidate set or any over-approximated ill-formed candidate narrows correct executions; selected invalid/no-match candidates keep the accepted runtime faults.
- **I31**: Creating an actual R call from a coherent event list would evade predication; reintroducing region-tier rejection loses inferred lifting.
- **I33**: Memoryless tuples for a memory-using body, treating stack cells as bytes or omitting replay/helper cost changes the fault set.
- **I34**: Rejecting a nonclosed unit rather than falling back narrows the fast path contract; running before final link without closedness can miss context.
- **I35**: Requiring devirtualisation or rewriting SQLite narrows scope; qjumpr is intra-function and cannot substitute for a call.
- **I36**: Blanket asm rejection removes musl/kernel paths; treating a syscall as a no-op silently changes effects; patterns do not constitute a completed platform inventory.
- **I37**: Fixed-arity-only acceptance or relying on host register-save contents excludes printf/sqlite3_mprintf and misreads front-end va_arg expansion.
- **I39**: Rejecting setjmp or turning volatile MMIO into an ordinary memfault drops platform scope; restricting translation to user mode breaks supervisor virtual memory.
- **I-0t9**: Silently redefining candidates to mean a chosen entry would break existing examples; editing accepted bytes to reapply an already-present fix is unnecessary.
- **I-0y2**: Ignoring the store, storing only the old result, or forcing TOP when the finite expansion is available loses the mandated materialised domain; weakening the single-thread assumption is outside this repair.
- **I-gwf**: Inventing schema fields, returning normally from a faulted R call or labelling a fixed-database subdomain full-D proof misstates ISA 0.9. Evidence still supports the rung's declared-space test; no rung is removed.

## Round-7 fixes — b-dialect-spec-j08 — 2026-10-30

Sole spec/checker editor; baseline 2651. Before edits, LLVM 18/23 probes
verified the original pointer/lane/FP sources at O0. Pointer arithmetic:
2*(-2^63)=0 modulo 2^64; wide +2^64 truncates to zero displacement.
Dynamic lane {1,3} plus totalised zero gives widths {1,2,4}. Constant index
2 (or unsigned -1) on two lanes extracts zero / preserves inserted vector.
fp128 -> x86_fp80 and ppc_fp128 -> fp128 fpext both fail with
`invalid cast opcode` on both LLVM majors. Direct own-format carrier calls
avoid these conversions entirely. Probe logs: scripts/.tmp/round7-probes.

## Decisions taken while writing (not in the outline)

- Primitives `__bennett_nz_alloc` / `__bennett_nz_free` (ISA alloc/free, lift.alloc/lift.free)
  added next to `__bennett_nz_fault`: the runtimes allocator needs a way to reach `lift.alloc`.
- Reserved-name rules apply to *producer inputs* (driver checks before link); runtimes/arith
  bitcode may use `__bennett_rt_/dev_/sf_/nz_` names.
- §5: abstract value = (atom set, TOP flag); TOP never stands for a ROOT atom; K = 4096 cap is
  normative (decides verdicts). Residue classes carry an extent [lo, hi) from array types (B-27).
- §5: `inttoptr` constants are TOP for function pointers (A(F) is fixed only after the
  comparison link); a Julia `@cfunction` constant traps unless it equals an A(F) at run time;
  Bennett.jl's `ptr @f` route keeps the capability.
- §6.5: two realisations: *direct* (handle never stored in memory: CC qreg SSA values, no bound)
  and *static register file* (stored handles; reference instance bound; infinite -> BLK-1).
- §6.6: device-entry pointer parameters get a candidate ROOT(E,i) atom that survives only if it
  reaches a marker handle operand (decides QREG binding).
- §7.5(b): R-tier allocation hoisting uses the reference instance bound; BLK-4 only when infinite.
- §8.1: descriptor layout = LLVM struct {H,[n x Bind],[m x DevBind]} under the datalayout.
- §8.5: snapshot register released by `measure` (unentangled basis state).
- §8.6: wide outputs are the `wide` event: copy-out pairs issued as CC-level region calls
  (`qreg.slice` views, `@xor<w>` action), temporaries freed with the ISA §3.3 dynamic check.
- §8.7: in-place verification computes B_min; run-time budgets checked at the marker (`T-BUDGET`).
- §9.2: budget table JSON schema and precedence (identity > region key > symbol glob > default).
- §9.5 example `budget-device-computed` uses a 64-bit value assembled from 64 measurements, so no
  launch-time token set covers it (a value set like {5, n+5} would be launch-mintable).
- §10: Cl/M/Co object states; slices with classical twins; events applied as CC-level region
  calls (ISA §6 per-region coarse windows make a static action unable to uncompute a slice after
  an arena write); per-slice fault registers retained and combined by `@firstfault`.
- §12.1: N33 runs immediately before N32 (its fpext/fptrunc pairs are FP that N32 rewrites).
- §14.9: blockaddress values are bytes of a driver-added data object `__bennett_rt_blk.<f>`, so
  they never collide with A(F) or other objects.
- §15.2: the default `cpuid` table is read on the build machine and recorded in the build record.
- §16: reference object = wrapper `@ref` + lprocs; layout restricted to closure-reachable
  globals; A_tab chosen so allocation-table overflow never precedes heap exhaustion.
- §18.4: `T-LEAK` outside generations is checked at program end (§6.6's REPL lifetime).
- §19.5: `text_base` rises above the device ranges when they pass 0x400000 (native binary must
  map heap/arena/regions disjointly from its code); §20.1 RAM placed by the profile's linker
  script at 0x80000000 after the other data.

## Departures from the outline

All are in the spec's Appendix A (A1-A23), each with its reason; every one keeps or widens the
outline's capability. Summary: A1 wide outputs by 2k-1 copy-out calls (outline's qxor cleanup is
ill-formed under ISA §6); A2 snapshot release by measure; A3 direct handle realisation without a
bound; A4 exact reference instance bound; A5 Cl/M/Co; A6 slices without stores/markers + classical
twins; A7 one XOR of c ⊕ v; A8 CC-level event application; A9 retained per-slice fault registers;
A10 effects in action regions are fault 8; A11 history as declared outputs measured at the
epilogue; A12 two more primitives; A13 `@cfunction` constants dispatched by value; A14 thunk cycles
resolve to themselves (BD-E-REGION-THUNK deleted); A15 N0 (LLVM's own lowering passes); A16 N34
marks as metadata; A17 wrapper/lproc form and layout rules; A18 compare-tree block names; A19
blockaddress/indirectbr, seven FP formats, exit via hostcall, B_min/T-BUDGET; A20 two more wording
items; A21 `__bennett_rt_platform_ram`; A22 `spec-sem2-*` beside `spec-sem-*`; A23 N33 before N32.

## V10 post-round correction (2026-10-29, b-dialect-spec-7u1)

The coverage-follow-up reports above describe the pre-correction 0.2.1 baseline.
This correction resolves the normative conflict, not the other freeze-gate gaps.

Before editing, re-derived both readings by hand and recorded them in a Beads note:

- Literal V10: load half and bitcast are exceptions, but fneg half is not, so the
  old residue witness rejects. The same reading also excludes the retained
  fabs/copysign calls and extended-format calls, returns and aggregate transport.
  Removing those forms would contradict §13.1's unchanged row, §13.3's all-seven-
  format contract, §16's carrier map and NS §3.2's bit-exact promise. It narrows scope.
- Retained-operation reading: N32/N33 remove arithmetic/comparison/conversion;
  §13.1's bit operations and §16's transport remain. For half carrier bits b,
  fneg is b xor 0x8000, including NaNs. Residual fadd half must still reject:
  its materialised replacement uses __bennett_sf_add_f16 on i16 carriers.

Deciding sentence: **V10 must permit every bit-exact operation retained by §13.1
and every carrier transport admitted by §16, for all seven floating-point formats.**
Rule 10 selects the second reading; there are not two non-narrowing alternatives.

Edited only the V10 exception row, its explanation/witnesses and Appendix B,
plus the version labels required by spec/README.md and §23. The positive now
retains fneg half; the negative retains fadd half instead. New indexed
validator-v10-carriers accepts fabs/copysign plus defined-call/return/aggregate
transport. V4/V9/V12 still apply to calls. §13.1 and §16.4 are unchanged.
Full dialect and norm advance to 0.2.2 because a normative rejection changed;
unchanged sub-artefacts, ISA 0.8, map 0.2.1, reference objects and hashes stay put.

Verification, headless, project TMPDIR, Python -B, LLVM stdin/stdout only:

- Reproduced the pre-edit mismatch: old V10 residue declared reject, checker accepts.
- All 190 tagged LLVM blocks verify on LLVM 18/20/23: 570/570.
- All three V10 verdicts match the read-only checker: accept/reject/accept.
- Seven-format probes cover retained bit operations, load/store/select/phi,
  bitcast, parameters, defined calls, returns and aggregate field transport;
  each accepts, and its fadd variant rejects. All 14 modules verify on all
  three majors (42/42). These are supplemental probes, not new spec examples.
- Independent LLVM instcombine folds agree with b xor 0x8000 on ten half bit
  patterns per major (30/30), including signed zero, infinities and signaling/
  quiet NaNs with nonzero payloads.
- Current 0.2 cross-reference checker: 1310/1310. The legacy 0.1 helper reports
  the same seven failures as e74d70c; it is not the current cross-reference gate.

### §1.1 What the dialect is   [DLT-1.1]

````text
DLT-1.1-P1
  <1>1 [req] The dialect is the contract between **front ends** that emit LLVM IR containing calls to `__bennett_*` marker functions and the **plugin** that, at the final link of a whole program, recognises those calls, analyses and normalises the code they reach, and maps it onto the ISA (ISA §1.1).   deps: ISA-1.1
  <1>2 [req] It fixes:
DLT-1.1-P2
  <1>1 [req] the marker ABI, operand encodings and C header (§3);   deps: DLT-3
DLT-1.1-P3
  <1>1 [req] the processing order, execution tiers, polyvariant variants and function addresses (§4);   deps: DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant), DLT-4.4-P1.S1 (function address), DLT-4
DLT-1.1-P4
  <1>1 [req] the device analysis: points-to, value sets and every question answered from them (§5);   deps: DLT-2-P10.S1 (value set), DLT-5
DLT-1.1-P5
  <1>1 [req] the handle convention, provenance, comparison and collections of handles (§6);   deps: DLT-6
DLT-1.1-P6
  <1>1 [req] regions: kinds, candidate sets, dispatch, identity, well-formedness (§7);   deps: DLT-7
DLT-1.1-P7
  <1>1 [req] the oracle interface: the descriptor, parameter and device bindings, entry state, wide outputs and in-place updates (§8);   deps: DLT-8
DLT-1.1-P8
  <1>1 [req] budgets (§9);   deps: DLT-9
DLT-1.1-P9
  <1>1 [req] taint-driven lifting of classical code under control (§10);   deps: DLT-10
DLT-1.1-P10
  <1>1 [req] effects and device models per tier (§11);   deps: DLT-11
DLT-1.1-P11
  <1>1 [req] the materialised normalisation and the residual-poison validator (§12), floating point (§13), calls and control transfer (§14), inline asm and target intrinsics (§15);   deps: DLT-12.2-P34.S1 (floating point), DLT-12, DLT-13, DLT-14, DLT-15
DLT-1.1-P12
  <1>1 [req] the lifting map from materialised LLVM to ISA objects (§16);   deps: DLT-16
DLT-1.1-P13
  <1>1 [req] the device classical memory model, CC and R lowering rules and fault outcomes (§17);   deps: DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC), DLT-17
DLT-1.1-P14
  <1>1 [req] a reference semantics from marker programs to the ISA formal model (§18);   deps: DLT-18
DLT-1.1-P15
  <1>1 [req] the driver's modes and plugin-invocation interface (§19);   deps: DLT-19
DLT-1.1-P16
  <1>1 [req] the platform profile `riscv64-bennett-virt` (§20);   deps: DLT-20
DLT-1.1-P17
  <1>1 [req] the legality corpus and conformance suites (§21); diagnostics (§22); versioning (§23); deferred mechanics (§24); blockers and ISA items (§25).   deps: DLT-21, DLT-22, DLT-23, DLT-24, DLT-25
DLT-1.1-P18
  <1>1 [req] It does not fix the plugin's optimisation pipeline after normalisation, the plugin's device objects beyond the constraints of §18.7, or any format the ISA owns.   deps: DLT-18.7
````

````text
DLT-1.2-P4

DLT-1.2-P5
  <1>1 [req] Runtime | `bennett-runtimes` and `bennett-arith` | define every entry point that §11, §13, §14, §17 and §20 name (prefixes `__bennett_rt_`, `__bennett_dev_`, `__bennett_sf_`, §3.1) with the semantics stated there, as ordinary bitcode compiled by the same pipeline; suites DR and DF   deps: DLT-21.3-P11.S1 (DR), DLT-11, DLT-13, DLT-14, DLT-17, DLT-20, DLT-3.1
DLT-1.2-P6
````

### §1.3 Relation to the ISA specification   [DLT-1.3]

````text
DLT-1.3-P1
  <1>1 [req] The ISA is settled; this document never redefines it.
  <1>2 [req] Every ISA notion used here (tiers, wires, `qreg` handles, oracles, actions, permutation actions, lprocs, F_B, budgets, tokens, fault codes, the reference interpreter, interface and closure hashes, layouts, the launch ABI) has exactly the meaning ISA §2–§17 give it.   deps: DLT-2-P3.S2 (wire), ISA-2, ISA-3, ISA-4, ISA-5, ISA-6, ISA-7, ISA-8, ISA-9, ISA-10, ISA-11, ISA-12, ISA-13, ISA-14, ISA-15, ISA-16, ISA-17
  <1>3 [req] Where the dialect needs a construct ISA 0.8 lacks, this document states (a) the full dialect mechanism, (b) its realisation on ISA 0.8 where one exists, which may be a longer construction (an **efficiency item**, §25.3), and (c) otherwise a **blocker** (§25.1) naming the exact ISA change.   deps: DLT-25.3, DLT-25.1
    <2>1 [req] (a) the full dialect mechanism
    <2>2 [req] (b) its realisation on ISA 0.8 where one exists, which may be a longer construction (an **efficiency item**, §25.3)   deps: DLT-25.3
    <2>3 [req] (c) otherwise a **blocker** (§25.1) naming the exact ISA change.   deps: DLT-25.1
  <1>4 [req] The dialect never shrinks to fit the ISA and never extends the ISA unilaterally.
````

### §1.6 Diagnostics and verdicts   [DLT-1.6]

````text
DLT-1.6-P1
  <1>1 [req] A module's **verdict** is one of:
DLT-1.6-P2
  <1>1 [req] `accept`: the plugin produces its objects;
DLT-1.6-P3
  <1>1 [req] `reject:<code>`: a compile-time rejection of §22.1.   deps: DLT-22.1
  <1>2 [req] The plugin MUST fail the compilation (nonzero exit, no output object) and report at least the first diagnostic in the processing order of §4.1;   deps: DLT-4.1
DLT-1.6-P4
  <1>1 [req] `blocked:<code>`: the module is accepted by the dialect, but at least one program point needs a capability that ISA 0.8 cannot express (§25.1).   deps: DLT-25.1
  <1>2 [req] The plugin MUST produce its objects with every such point lowered to a **blocker trap** (§25.1: a run-time fault on exactly the executions that reach the point), MUST emit the blocker report of §25.1 and MUST exit with the distinct status 3.   deps: DLT-2-P15.S1 (lowered), DLT-25.1
  <1>3 [req] The code is the first blocker report in processing order.
DLT-1.6-P5
  <1>1 [req] The R-entry BLK-5 classification of §11.5 and §25.1 applies even when all supplied budgets allow a successful execution; §17.6 defines its mandatory typed fault point.   deps: DLT-25.1-P4.S1 (BLK-5), DLT-11.5, DLT-25.1, DLT-17.6
DLT-1.6-P6
  <1>1 [req] A module that would be rejected and blocked is rejected.
  <1>2 [req] Warnings (`BD-W-*`, §22.4) never change a verdict.   deps: DLT-22.4
````

### §2 Terminology   [DLT-2]

````text
DLT-2-P1
  <1>1 [def] **Marker**: one of the 23 functions of §3.2.   deps: DLT-3.2
  <1>2 [def] **Marker call**: a `call` or `invoke` whose callee is a marker (§3.5).   deps: DLT-3.5
  <1>3 [def] **Effect marker**: one of the five `__bennett_effect_*` markers.
DLT-2-P2
  <1>1 [def] **Primitive**: a reserved function with prefix `__bennett_nz_` that the map lowers to an ISA instruction directly (§3.1, §16.4): `__bennett_nz_fault`, `__bennett_nz_alloc`, `__bennett_nz_free`.   deps: DLT-3.1, DLT-16.4
  <1>2 [def] **Runtime entry point**: a function with prefix `__bennett_rt_`, `__bennett_dev_` or `__bennett_sf_` that `bennett-runtimes` or `bennett-arith` defines in bitcode (§3.1).   deps: DLT-3.1
DLT-2-P3
  <1>1 [def] **Handle**: the `ptr` value a `__bennett_qalloc` or `__bennett_qborrow` call returns; it denotes a **register** of n qubits, the ISA's `qreg[n]` (ISA §3.3).   deps: ISA-3.3
  <1>2 [def] Qubit `i` of a handle is a **wire**.
  <1>3 [def] **Register tag**: the opaque value (nonzero, below 2^pw) that represents a handle in device memory and in integers; at the host–device boundary a handle is an ISA launch register id (§6.1).   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register), DLT-6.1
DLT-2-P4
  <1>1 [def] **Root**: an allocation of a register, identified by its allocation site and dynamic instance index (§6.5).   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register), DLT-5.1-P4.S1 (allocation site), DLT-6.5
  <1>2 [def] **Handle-derived**: a value whose provenance (§6.2) contains a root.   deps: DLT-6.2
DLT-2-P5
  <1>1 [def] **Region function**: a function a region-entry marker receives.
  <1>2 [def] **Region operand**: the marker operand that names it.
  <1>3 [def] **Candidate set**: the functions a region operand can denote (§7.2).   deps: DLT-7.2
DLT-2-P6
  <1>1 [def] **Action region**: a candidate of a `ctrl`, `adj` or `compute` operand; its interface is a quantum action (ISA §5.3).   deps: ISA-5.3
  <1>2 [def] **Oracle region**: a candidate of an `oracle` or `inplace` operand; its interface is a lifted oracle (ISA §5.2).   deps: ISA-5.2
  <1>3 [def] **Reversible region**: a candidate of a `reversible` operand, or the whole-program entry of §19.2; R-tier code (ISA §3.1).   deps: DLT-19.2, ISA-3.1
DLT-2-P7
  <1>1 [def] **Tier** of a function variant: **H** (host, native), **CC** (device classical control, ISA §3.1), **R** (reversible, ISA §3.1), **L** (lifted: an lproc or oracle body, ISA §3.7).   deps: DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant), ISA-3.1, ISA-3.7
  <1>2 [def] A **variant** is a (function, tier, coherence signature) triple (§4.3); host code keeps the original function, every device tier gets a clone.   deps: DLT-4.3
DLT-2-P8
  <1>1 [def] **Device program**: every variant of tier CC, R or L.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant), DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC)
  <1>2 [def] **Device entry**: a device variant called by an H function (a launch, ISA §10).   deps: DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant), ISA-10
DLT-2-P9
  <1>1 [def] **Function address** A(F): the address of F in the driver's comparison link (§4.4).   deps: DLT-4.4-P1.S1 (comparison link), DLT-4.4
DLT-2-P10
  <1>1 [req] **Abstract object**, **slot**, **value set**: §5. ⊤ is the unbounded value set.   deps: DLT-5
DLT-2-P11
  <1>1 [def] **Descriptor**: the in-memory oracle interface record of §8.1.   deps: DLT-8.1
  <1>2 [def] **Binding**: one parameter or device entry of a descriptor.
  <1>3 [def] **Shape**: a tuple of binding kinds, modes and widths (§8.4).   deps: DLT-8.4
DLT-2-P12
  <1>1 [def] **Budget record**: the in-memory record `bennett_budget` of §9.1.   deps: DLT-9.1
  <1>2 [def] **Budget table**: the driver input of §9.2.   deps: DLT-9.2
DLT-2-P13
  <1>1 [def] **Coherence state**: Cl (classical) or Co (coherent) of a value or object instance (§10, TDL-2).   deps: DLT-10-P3.S1 (TDL-2), DLT-10
  <1>2 [def] **Coherent slice**: an outlined maximal region of Co instructions (TDL-3).   deps: DLT-10-P14.S1 (TDL-3)
  <1>3 [def] **Arena**: the coherent memory of §10 TDL-4.   deps: DLT-10-P19.S1 (TDL-4), DLT-10
  <1>4 [def] **Generation**: the classical execution of an action region that records its events (§18.4).   deps: DLT-7.1-P7.S3 (action region), DLT-18.4
DLT-2-P14
  <1>1 [def] **Device model**: one of `console`, `clock`, `entropy`, `block` (ISA §7.3), realised per tier by §11.   deps: ISA-7.3, DLT-11
DLT-2-P15
  <1>1 [req] **Coverage classes** (ISA §13): **lowered** (the construct has an ISA realisation), **shimmed** (it is replaced by a runtime or platform shim with a recorded `shim_hash`), **trapped** (it faults with code 8, `FAULT_EFFECT_UNMODELLED`, on the executions that reach it, and has a coverage line).   deps: ISA-13
DLT-2-P16
  <1>1 [def] **Driver mode**: one of the invocation modes of §19.2–§19.7.   deps: DLT-19.2, DLT-19.3, DLT-19.4, DLT-19.5, DLT-19.6, DLT-19.7
  <1>2 [def] **Platform profile**: §20.   deps: DLT-20
DLT-2-P17
  <1>1 [def] **Materialised module**: the module after normalisation (§12).   deps: DLT-12
  <1>2 [def] **Reference object**: the ISA object the map produces for one oracle shape (§16.2); its oracle `@ref` defines F_B.   deps: DLT-16.2
DLT-2-P18
  <1>1 [def] **Blocker**: a capability with no ISA 0.8 realisation in a stated case (§25.1), BLK-1, BLK-2, BLK-4 and BLK-5 (BLK-3 retired, §25.1).   deps: DLT-25.1-P2.S1 (BLK-1), DLT-25.1-P3.S1 (BLK-2), DLT-25.1-P5.S1 (BLK-4), DLT-25.1-P4.S1 (BLK-5), DLT-25.1
````

````text
  <1>3 [req] A marker call is accepted iff all of the following hold; otherwise `BD-E-MARKER-SIGNATURE`:   deps: DLT-22.1-P6.S1 (BD-E-MARKER-SIGNATURE), DLT-3.5-P1.S1 (marker call)
````

### §3.6 The positive legality requirement and attributes   [DLT-3.6]

````text
DLT-3.6-P1
  <1>1 [req] A marker is an external declaration that may read and write any memory, may unwind and may not return: exactly an unknown external function to LLVM.
  <1>2 [req] Stock passes then preserve the dynamic sequence of marker calls on every executed path (spike findings §1: every standard pipeline of LLVM 18, 20 and 23, all 50 legal cases; the four negative controls are detected).   deps: DLT-10-P18.S1 (marker calls)
  <1>3 [req] No attribute is needed and none may be added that licenses elimination, commoning, speculation or motion.
DLT-3.6-P2
  <1>1 [req] Every attribute, keyword and calling convention on a marker declaration or marker call site is in exactly one of three lists:   deps: DLT-3.5-P1.S1 (marker call)
DLT-3.6-P3
  <1>1 [req] **Forbidden** (`BD-E-MARKER-ATTRIBUTE`): attributes that license motion or elimination: `memory(...)` in any form, `readnone`, `readonly`, `writeonly`, `argmemonly`, `inaccessiblememonly`, `inaccessiblemem_or_argmemonly`, `willreturn`, `speculatable`, `noreturn`, `returned`, `nocapture`, `captures(...)`, `dereferenceable(...)`, `dereferenceable_or_null(...)`, `align`, `nofpclass(...)`, `byval`, `sret`, `writable`, `initializes(...)`, `dead_on_unwind`, `nosync`, `nofree`, `norecurse`, `mustprogress`, `musttail`, any non-default calling convention, `extern_weak` linkage.   deps: DLT-22.1-P7.S1 (BD-E-MARKER-ATTRIBUTE)
  <1>2 [non] *(non-normative)* The first eight are the spike's L2 forbidden set; `noreturn` would delete the code after a marker; `returned` would replace a marker result by an argument; the parameter-effect attributes would let LLVM move stores to an environment across a region call; `dereferenceable` would let it speculate loads through a handle.   deps: DLT-21.1-P3.S1 (L2)
DLT-3.6-P4
  <1>1 [req] **Benign** (ignored): function position `nounwind`, `nonlazybind`, `uwtable` (any form), `strictfp`, `cold`, `hot`, `nomerge`, `noinline`, `convergent`, `builtin`, `nobuiltin`, `optsize`, `minsize`, `optnone`, and every string attribute; return and parameter position `noundef`, `nonnull`, `range(...)`, `zeroext`, `signext`; declaration linkage and keywords external linkage, `dso_local`, `dso_preemptable`, `unnamed_addr`, `local_unnamed_addr`, any visibility; call-site keywords `tail`, `notail`; instruction metadata of any kind.
  <1>2 [req] The first group is the spike's L2 evidence (findings §1, §4: front ends add `nounwind`, `nonlazybind`, `uwtable`, `noundef`, `nonnull`, `zeroext` and string attributes; passes add `local_unnamed_addr`, `nonnull`, `noundef`, `range`, `tail`).   deps: DLT-21.1-P3.S1 (L2), DLT-1.1-P1.S1 (front ends)
  <1>3 [req] `strictfp` through `optnone` are added by build flags NS §0 allows (`-ffp-model=strict`, `-Os`, `-O0`) or restrict motion; none licenses elimination, commoning, speculation or motion of an unknown call.
  <1>4 [req] Before this version freezes, a corpus run confirms each of them on the three majors (§21.2, bd `.21`).   deps: DLT-21.2
DLT-3.6-P5
  <1>1 [req] **Unknown**: every other attribute is `BD-E-MARKER-ATTRIBUTE` until corpus evidence moves it to one of the lists above with a version change.   deps: DLT-22.1-P7.S1 (BD-E-MARKER-ATTRIBUTE)
  <1>2 [req] This is required by NS §3.1 (the positive legality requirement: an attribute the dialect has not classified may license motion).
DLT-3.6-P6
  <1>1 [req] Attribute groups (`#N`) are resolved before the check.
  <1>2 [ex] (code block, 16 lines) declare ptr @__bennett_qalloc(i64 noundef, i64 noundef) unnamed_addr #0
DLT-3.6-P7
  <1>1 [req] Call sites under `-ffp-model=strict` carry `strictfp`; a `cold` declaration is benign too:
  <1>2 [ex] (code block, 13 lines) declare void @__bennett_rot(i32, ptr, i64, double) #0
  <1>3 [ex] (code block, 12 lines) declare void @__bennett_gate(i32, ptr, i64) #0   deps: DLT-22.1-P7.S1 (BD-E-MARKER-ATTRIBUTE)
  <1>4 [ex] (code block, 10 lines) define void @g() {   deps: DLT-22.1-P7.S1 (BD-E-MARKER-ATTRIBUTE)
DLT-3.6-P8
  <1>1 [req] The benign, forbidden and unknown marker-attribute classification MUST retain the accepted list and be checked against dynamic marker-sequence preservation on every supported LLVM major.   declared: DLT-3.6, DLT-21.1, DLT-21.2, ISA-13
````

### §3.7 Unwinding of markers   [DLT-3.7]

````text
DLT-3.7-P1
  <1>1 [req] Markers never unwind.   deps: DLT-2-P1.S1 (Marker)
  <1>2 [req] Before any other analysis (§4.1 step S1) the plugin rewrites every `invoke` of a marker into a `call` with the same operands followed by `br label %normal`, removes the invoking block from the phi nodes of the unwind destination, and then deletes every block not reachable from the function's entry.   deps: DLT-4.1-P2.S1 (S1), DLT-4.1
  <1>3 [non] *(non-normative)* This is Enzyme's practice (enzyme survey §1.1); C++ with `-fexceptions` and Rust `extern "C-unwind"` produce such invokes (emission summary item 3).   deps: DLT-1.1
  <1>4 [req] Front ends SHOULD declare markers non-unwinding (`noexcept`, Rust `extern "C"`).
  <1>5 [req] Unwinding through every other call of device code is the explicit-propagation transform of §14.4; 0.1's `BD-E-EH` is deleted.   deps: DLT-14.4
  <1>6 [ex] (code block, 18 lines) declare i32 @__gxx_personality_v0(...)
````

### §3.8 Front-end emission routes   [DLT-3.8]

````text
DLT-3.8-P1
  <1>1 [req] **clang (C, C++)** and **rustc** emit markers as direct calls to the declaration (emission summary).
  <1>2 [req] Rust MUST declare each marker with one ABI per crate (`extern "C"`); mixed `"C"`/`"C-unwind"` declarations are merged by rustc into one declaration with `invoke` call sites, which §3.7 accepts.   deps: DLT-3.7
DLT-3.8-P2
  <1>1 [req] **Julia** MUST emit markers with `ccall("extern __bennett_<name>", llvmcall, …)` or with `Base.llvmcall((module_ir, "entry"), …)` whose module contains the `declare`.
  <1>2 [req] Both give a direct call to an attribute-free declaration; `ccall("extern __bennett_measure", llvmcall, Bool, …)` gives `declare i1 @__bennett_measure(ptr, i64)`, exactly the §3.2 signature (verified with Julia 1.13.3).   deps: DLT-3.2
  <1>3 [req] A plain `ccall(:__bennett_x, …)` or `@ccall` is an indirect call through a `jlplt` GOT global and is not a marker call.   deps: DLT-3.5-P1.S1 (marker call)

DLT-3.8-P3
  <1>1 [def] **Region functions** are passed as `ptr @f` or as any value whose value set §7.2 resolves.   deps: DLT-2-P10.S1 (value set), DLT-7.2
  <1>2 [req] Bennett.jl emits `ptr @f` in its own module (LLVM.jl), which keeps the full capability (audit B-14).
  <1>3 [req] A Julia `@cfunction` pointer is an `inttoptr` constant of an address of the Julia process; like every region pointer with value set ⊤ it is dispatched by value against the address-taken functions of the required type (§7.2), and an execution on which it equals no A(F) traps (`T-REGION`).   deps: DLT-2-P10.S1 (value set), DLT-7.2
DLT-3.8-P4
  <1>1 [def] **Descriptors and budget records** are built by plain stores into an `alloca` or global (C: the header macros; Rust: `#[repr(C)]` structs; Julia: `Ref` of an `isbits` struct), which survive `default<O3>` as constant stores that §5.3 reads (corpus cases, §21.2).   deps: DLT-5.3, DLT-21.2
DLT-3.8-P5
  <1>1 [req] **Source effect lies** (spike F5). A device function definition carrying any of `memory(none)`, `memory(read)` (any `memory(...)` whose effects exclude a write to any location), `readnone`, `readonly`, `willreturn` or `speculatable`, from which a marker call is reachable through the call graph of §4.1 (the function itself included), is `BD-E-EFFECT-LIE`.   deps: DLT-22.1-P9.S1 (BD-E-EFFECT-LIE), DLT-3.5-P1.S1 (marker call), DLT-4.1-P12.S1 (call graph), DLT-4.1
  <1>2 [non] *(non-normative)* LLVM cannot infer these attributes for a function that reaches an unknown external call, so they come from the source; the front end's own optimiser may already have deleted marker calls on their strength, which is why this is a diagnostic and not a guarantee (definedness assumption, NS §3.2).   deps: DLT-10-P18.S1 (marker calls)
  <1>3 [ex] (code block, 11 lines) @jlplt___bennett_gate_528_got = external global ptr #0   deps: DLT-22.1-P8.S1 (BD-E-JULIA-CCALL)
  <1>4 [ex] (code block, 15 lines) define internal void @kick(ptr %h) #0 {   deps: DLT-22.1-P9.S1 (BD-E-EFFECT-LIE)
````

### §4.1 Processing order   [DLT-4.1]

````text
DLT-4.1-P1
  <1>1 [req] A plugin processes the whole-program module (after the driver's link and post-link pipeline, §19.1) in this order; the first failing rule gives the verdict (§1.6):   deps: DLT-19.1, DLT-1.6
DLT-4.1-P2
  <1>1 [req] S1 | §3.1 reserved names; §3.5 recognition; §3.6 attributes; §3.8 Julia check; §3.7 marker invokes; §3.8 effect lies; §19.9 version checks   deps: DLT-3.1, DLT-3.5, DLT-3.6, DLT-3.8, DLT-3.7, DLT-19.9
DLT-4.1-P3
  <1>1 [req] S2 | the device analysis (§5): one fixpoint for points-to, value sets, region candidates (§7.2), indirect-call candidates (§14.2), handle provenance (§6.2) and descriptor kinds (§8.4)   deps: DLT-2-P10.S1 (value set), DLT-5, DLT-7.2, DLT-14.2, DLT-6.2, DLT-8.4
DLT-4.1-P4
  <1>1 [req] S3 | tier assignment and variants (§4.2–§4.4); calls out of the device program (§4.5)   deps: DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant), DLT-4.2, DLT-4.3, DLT-4.4, DLT-4.5
DLT-4.1-P5
  <1>1 [def] S4 | handle rules (§6)   deps: DLT-6
DLT-4.1-P6
  <1>1 [def] S5 | region well-formedness (§7.5)   deps: DLT-7.5
DLT-4.1-P7
  <1>1 [req] S6 | the TDL partition and the may-Co analysis (§10)   deps: DLT-10
DLT-4.1-P8
  <1>1 [def] S7 | normalisation of every device variant (§12) and the residual-poison validator (§12.4); dispatch domains (§3.4)   deps: DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant), DLT-3.4-P20.S3 (dispatch domain), DLT-12, DLT-12.4, DLT-3.4
DLT-4.1-P9
  <1>1 [def] S8 | lifting (§16) of every oracle shape and coherent slice; in-place verification (§8.7)   deps: DLT-16, DLT-8.7
DLT-4.1-P10
  <1>1 [req] S9 | lowering to ISA objects (§17; plugin-defined, constrained by §18.7); blocker reports (§25.1)   deps: DLT-17, DLT-18.7, DLT-25.1
DLT-4.1-P11
  <1>1 [req] Within a step, rules apply in the order listed; within a rule, to instructions in module text order.
  <1>2 [req] Blocker reports are collected during S2–S8 and issued in S9 in that order.   deps: DLT-4.1-P3.S1 (S2), DLT-4.1-P4.S1 (S3), DLT-4.1-P5.S1 (S4), DLT-4.1-P6.S1 (S5), DLT-4.1-P7.S1 (S6), DLT-4.1-P8.S1 (S7), DLT-4.1-P9.S1 (S8), DLT-4.1-P10.S1 (S9), DLT-25.1-P8.S1 (Blocker report)
DLT-4.1-P12
  <1>1 [req] The **call graph** has an edge F → G when F contains a direct `call` or `invoke` of G (after resolving aliases), an edge F → R for every candidate R of every region operand of a marker call in F (a **region edge**), and an edge F → C for every candidate C of every indirect call in F (§14.2).   deps: DLT-14.2
  <1>2 [req] Only functions with a definition are nodes.
  <1>3 [req] The **closure** of a function is the set of functions reachable from it by direct and indirect-candidate edges (region edges start a new region and are not followed).   deps: DLT-4.1-P12.S1 (region edge)
````

### §4.2 Tier assignment   [DLT-4.2]

````text
DLT-4.2-P1
  <1>1 [req] Every defined function reachable from the program's roots gets a set of tiers.
  <1>2 [def] The **host roots** are the functions with non-local linkage and the functions whose address host code uses; the **device roots** are the region candidates and the whole-program entry of §19.2.   deps: DLT-19.2
DLT-4.2-P2
  <1>1 [req] **CC**: a function that contains a marker call, receives a handle (a parameter or a loaded value whose provenance contains a root, §6.2), is a candidate of an action region operand (its classical part is the generation, §18.4), is a device entry, is in the CC closure of one of these, or is promoted by §19.4.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC), DLT-3.5-P1.S1 (marker call), DLT-7.1-P7.S3 (action region), DLT-6.2, DLT-18.4, DLT-19.4
DLT-4.2-P3
  <1>1 [req] **R**: a function in the closure of a `reversible` region operand, or every function under `--bennett-tier=reversible` (§19.2).   deps: DLT-19.2
DLT-4.2-P4
  <1>1 [req] **L**: a function in the closure of an oracle or in-place region operand, or of a coherent slice (§10, TDL-3).   deps: DLT-10-P14.S1 (TDL-3), DLT-10
DLT-4.2-P5
  <1>1 [req] **H**: every other function reachable from a host root, and every function reachable from a host root through host code only.
  <1>2 [req] A function in no device tier stays H only.
DLT-4.2-P6
  <1>1 [req] A function may get several tiers; it then has one variant per tier (§4.3).   deps: DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant), DLT-4.3
  <1>2 [non] *(non-normative)* SQLite in the rung-4 program is H (the host builds and serialises the database) and L (the oracle runs the query), so it has two variants and one set of globals (SQLite §5.2(i)).   deps: DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant)
````

### §4.3 Polyvariant cloning   [DLT-4.3]

````text
DLT-4.3-P1
  <1>1 [req] A **variant** is a (function, tier, coherence signature) triple, where the coherence signature is the tuple of coherence states of the function's parameters and of the may-Co objects it reads (§10, TDL-2) and is empty outside TDL.   deps: DLT-10-P3.S1 (TDL-2), DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant), DLT-10
  <1>2 [req] The H variant is the original function; every device variant is a clone.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant)
  <1>3 [req] **Clones share every global: data is never cloned.**
  <1>4 [req] There is one classical memory (NS §3.2), shared by H, CC, R and the entry state of every L invocation (§8.5).   deps: DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC), DLT-8.5
  <1>5 [req] Calls inside a variant call the variant of the callee with the caller's tier and the coherence signature at the call.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant)
  <1>6 [req] 0.1's `BD-E-DEVICE-ADDRESS` is deleted: a host function may take the address of any function (audit B-16).
````

### §4.4 Function addresses   [DLT-4.4]

````text
DLT-4.4-P1
  <1>1 [req] Every function whose address is used has the **function address** A(F): its address in the driver's **comparison link** (§19.5: non-PIE, fixed section addresses, identical-code folding and constant merging off; NS §3.2, SQLite §5.2(ii)).   deps: DLT-19.5
  <1>2 [req] A(F) is the value of `ptr @F` in every tier:
DLT-4.4-P2
  <1>1 [req] in host code, by linking the production host image with the comparison layout whenever an address may cross the host–device boundary (§19.5);   deps: DLT-19.5
DLT-4.4-P3
  <1>1 [req] in CC and R code, as `const` plus `inttoptr` (ISA §4.1);   deps: DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC), ISA-4.1
DLT-4.4-P4
  <1>1 [req] in lifted code, as `lift.const` (ISA §4.2);   deps: ISA-4.2
DLT-4.4-P5
  <1>1 [req] in every data image: global initialisers, vtables, function tables (SQLite's `aBuiltinFunc`, VFS and pcache method tables).
DLT-4.4-P6
  <1>1 [unc] So `ptrtoint`, comparison, hashing and storage of function pointers equal native execution.
  <1>2 [req] Each tier maps A(F) to its own variant of F by the dispatch of §14.2.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant), DLT-14.2
  <1>3 [req] Two functions never have equal A(F) (identical-code folding is off), so the map is well defined.
  <1>4 [req] A `blockaddress` constant is §14.9.   deps: DLT-14.9
DLT-4.4-P7
  <1>1 [req] Host and device variants MUST retain a common comparison-link function address and shared global data, while dispatch selects the variant for the caller's tier and coherence signature.   deps: ~DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant), DLT-4.4-P1.S1 (function address)   declared: DLT-4.3-P1, DLT-4.4, DLT-19.5, ISA-4.1, ISA-4.2, ISA-9.1
````

### §4.5 Calls out of the device program   [DLT-4.5]

````text
DLT-4.5-P1
  <1>1 [req] A call in a device variant of a function with no definition resolves, in this order:   deps: DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant)
DLT-4.5-P2
  <1>1 [req] a marker (§3.2) or a primitive (§3.1);   deps: DLT-3.2, DLT-3.1
DLT-4.5-P3
  <1>1 [def] a **runtime shim**: a definition of the symbol in `bennett-runtimes` or `bennett-arith` bitcode, which the driver links before S2 (§19.1): libc and libm (musl-derived), libpthread with one thread, the Julia shim runtime, Rust's `core::panicking::*` targets and the platform shims of §20.   deps: DLT-4.1-P3.S1 (S2), DLT-19.1, DLT-20
  <1>2 [req] The shim is an ordinary device function (coverage class `shimmed`, with its `shim_hash`, ISA §13);   deps: DLT-2-P15.S1 (shimmed), ISA-13
DLT-4.5-P4
  <1>1 [def] in a CC variant only, a **host call** through `hostcall` (§11.4);   deps: DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC), DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant), DLT-11.4
DLT-4.5-P5
  <1>1 [req] otherwise **trapped**: the call is replaced by F(8) (§12.3) and the coverage report has a `trapped` line for it (NS §3.3: "Calls with no bitcode are coverage-report lines (*trapped*), never silent").   deps: DLT-2-P15.S1 (trapped), DLT-12.3
DLT-4.5-P6
  <1>1 [req] An R or L variant never makes a host call (ISA §4.1: `hostcall` is CC only; NS §4.2: coherent regions are closed).   deps: DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant), DLT-4.5-P4.S1 (host call), DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC), ISA-4.1
  <1>2 [non] *(non-normative)* Item 4 is the only fault the dialect introduces for a call, and it occurs only on the executions that reach the call; it is the north star's own rule.
````

### §5 The device analysis (one fixpoint)   [DLT-5]

````text
DLT-5-P1
  <1>1 [req] The device analysis is a whole-program, flow-insensitive, inclusion-based (Andersen-style), field-sensitive points-to and value-set analysis over every device variant and every host function that exchanges data with one (passes it a pointer, or shares a global it accesses).   deps: DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant)
  <1>2 [req] It is specified exactly: **every verdict, candidate set and dispatch domain of this document is computed from the reference analysis below.**   deps: DLT-3.4-P20.S3 (dispatch domain)
  <1>3 [req] A plugin MAY use a more precise analysis to shrink dispatch domains or arena placement in its lowering, never to change a verdict (the run-time value is always a member of the reference set, so the results are unchanged).   deps: DLT-3.4-P20.S3 (dispatch domain)
````

### §5.1 Abstract objects and atoms   [DLT-5.1]

````text
DLT-5.1-P1
  <1>1 [def] The **abstract objects** are:
DLT-5.1-P2
  <1>1 [def] each `alloca` instruction;
DLT-5.1-P3
  <1>1 [def] each global variable;
DLT-5.1-P4
  <1>1 [def] each **allocation site**: a call of a function that carries `allockind("alloc")` or `allocsize(...)`, or whose name is one of `malloc`, `calloc`, `realloc`, `aligned_alloc`, `posix_memalign` (the object is the one written through its first argument), `memalign`, `strdup`, `strndup`, `_Znwm`, `_Znam`, `_ZnwmRKSt9nothrow_t`, `_ZnamRKSt9nothrow_t`, `_ZnwmSt11align_val_t`, `_ZnamSt11align_val_t`, `__rust_alloc`, `__rust_alloc_zeroed`, `__rust_realloc`, `julia.gc_alloc_obj`, `ijl_gc_alloc_typed`, `jl_gc_alloc`, `ijl_gc_small_alloc`, `ijl_gc_big_alloc`, or `__bennett_nz_alloc`;
DLT-5.1-P5
  <1>1 [req] the pseudo-object `EXT` (memory of unknown provenance: host memory reached through a pointer the analysis did not create).
DLT-5.1-P6
  <1>1 [req] Heap objects are context-insensitive: one object per allocation-site instruction of the variant in which it occurs.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant)
  <1>2 [req] The list above is the reference list; `bennett-runtimes` declares its allocator entry points with `allockind("alloc")` so that they are covered by the first rule.
DLT-5.1-P7
  <1>1 [req] An **offset** is an integer byte offset, a **residue class** (r mod s)[lo, hi) with s ≥ 2 (every offset o with o ≡ r (mod s) and lo ≤ o < hi), or `*` (any offset).
  <1>2 [req] An **atom** is one of:
DLT-5.1-P8
  <1>1 [req] `(X, o)`: a pointer into object X at offset o;
DLT-5.1-P9
  <1>1 [req] `FN(F)`: the address A(F) of a defined function F;
DLT-5.1-P10
  <1>1 [req] `ROOT(r)`: a handle with root r (the allocation site of a `qalloc`/`qborrow` call, §6.5);   deps: DLT-5.1-P4.S1 (allocation site), DLT-6.5
DLT-5.1-P11
  <1>1 [req] `INT(c)`: the integer constant c (of the value's width).
DLT-5.1-P12
  <1>1 [req] Every SSA value v (per lane for vectors, per index path for aggregates) has an **abstract value** AV(v) = (A, t): a finite set A of atoms and a flag t; t = ⊤ means "and any other integer or address". ⊤ never stands for a `ROOT` atom (handle provenance is always explicit); for a function-pointer operand it stands for "any function of the operand's type whose address is used" (§7.2, §14.2).   deps: DLT-7.2, DLT-14.2
  <1>2 [req] Every slot (X, o) of memory has a content AV(X, o) of the same form.   deps: DLT-2-P10.S1 (slot)
  <1>3 [req] When A holds more than **K = 4096** `INT` atoms they are dropped and t is set (a normative constant: it decides dispatch and blocker verdicts, so §24 does not defer it).   deps: DLT-24
  <1>4 [req] "AV(v) = ⊤" below means t is set; unions and inclusions are taken component-wise.
DLT-5.1-P13
  <1>1 [req] Abstract-object and return propagation MUST cover attributed allocator calls and defined allocator wrappers through their underlying allocation sites without requiring the wrapper's name in a whitelist.   deps: DLT-5.1-P4.S1 (allocation site)   declared: DLT-5.1-P4, DLT-5.1-P6, DLT-5.2-P10, ISA-7.1, ISA-7.2
````

### §5.2 Rules   [DLT-5.2]

````text
DLT-5.2-P1
  <1>1 [unc] Before the fixpoint, seed the initialiser atoms of every global, mutable or constant, into its slots.   deps: DLT-2-P10.S1 (slot)
  <1>2 [req] For each alloca and allocation-site object, also represent every extent whose initial contents are zero under §§17.1/17.3 as a zero-byte initial image; represent a nonconstant extent symbolically over its possible allocated bytes.   deps: DLT-17.1, DLT-17.3
  <1>3 [req] Subsequent stores union additional possibilities and never erase these initial possibilities.
  <1>4 [req] This is an initial image, not a claim that the object remains immutable.
  <1>5 [req] The analysis is the least fixpoint of the following rules over AV.
  <1>6 [req] "Copies" means AV(result) ⊇ AV(operand) lane by lane; ⊤ absorbs.
  <1>7 [req] S2 models the value effects of the specified normalisation before verdicts and dispatch domains freeze; pre-normalisation syntax does not permit omitting a value produced by the materialised execution.   deps: DLT-4.1-P3.S1 (S2), DLT-3.4-P20.S3 (dispatch domain)
DLT-5.2-P2
  <1>1 [req] PT1 | `alloca`, global `@G`, allocation-site call | AV ∋ (X, 0); zero-filled initial extents are seeded as above
DLT-5.2-P3
  <1>1 [req] PT2 | `getelementptr T, ptr p, idx…` | uses P(a), I(a) and the complete finite-width computation of §16.4, also for constant expressions: sequential indices are sign-extended/truncated to I(a), scaling and offset accumulation wrap modulo 2^I(a), and addition preserves pointer bits above I(a).   deps: DLT-16.4
  <1>2 [req] Zero accumulated offset copies AV(p).
  <1>3 [req] For every (X,o), include the image of all represented base addresses and index values (unknown base bits range over patterns consistent with DataLayout and X's alignment), using integer/residue-class/`*` offset unions.
  <1>4 [req] Unbounded mathematical addition is not a substitute.
  <1>5 [req] If an address may leave X, include (EXT, `*`) and the non-handle top flag; PT6 propagates this unknown-address alternative.   deps: DLT-5.2-P7.S1 (PT6)
  <1>6 [req] The unknown-address alternative does not by itself establish host escape (§6.4): retain the original base provenance for that test; actual host/unknown origins keep their restrictions.   deps: DLT-6.4
  <1>7 [req] ROOT provenance and §6.2 restrictions remain explicit.   deps: DLT-6.2
  <1>8 [req] Array dimensions determine stride, never an index bound
DLT-5.2-P4
  <1>1 [def] PT3 | `phi`, `select` (value operands), `freeze`, `addrspacecast`; `bitcast` | the first four copy (union).
  <1>2 [req] A bitcast copies lane by lane only when source and destination have identical lane counts and per-lane representation widths, treating a scalar as one lane.
  <1>3 [req] Otherwise use the virtual N21 bitcast expansion of §12.6: pack source-lane bit patterns into its prescribed bit string in DataLayout order, then resegment at the destination representation width.   deps: DLT-12.2-P23.S1 (N21), DLT-12.6
  <1>4 [req] Compute output AV through PT4/PT5 transfers of that expansion; finite INT lane sets denote their full Cartesian product, and K applies per resulting lane.   deps: DLT-5.2-P5.S1 (PT4), DLT-5.2-P6.S1 (PT5)
  <1>5 [req] Never copy a source-lane INT atom as the value of a packed destination scalar.
  <1>6 [req] Unknown bits propagate non-handle top through those transfers.
  <1>7 [req] Explicit object and ROOT provenance follows the same expansion and remains subject to §6.2; top never substitutes for ROOT.   deps: DLT-6.2
  <1>8 [req] Apply also to constant expressions and fixed-vscale forms during S2 before verdicts, candidate sets, shapes and dispatch domains freeze.   deps: DLT-4.1-P3.S1 (S2), DLT-3.4-P20.S3 (dispatch domain)
  <1>9 [req] Direct finite bit-string evaluation is equivalent; no LLVM optimisation is required
DLT-5.2-P5
  <1>1 [def] PT4 | `ptrtoint`, `inttoptr`, `zext`/`sext`/`trunc` | copy only bit-preserving conversions.
  <1>2 [req] Otherwise apply the actual source/destination-width bit-vector conversion (§16.4): ptrtoint/inttoptr zero-extend or truncate at P(a), sext sign-extends.   deps: DLT-16.4
  <1>3 [req] Use PT2’s represented-address image construction, retaining originating object and ROOT provenance.   deps: DLT-5.2-P3.S1 (PT2)
  <1>4 [req] A narrowed representation that cannot be reassociated with its original object adds (EXT, `*`) and non-handle ⊤; numerical uncertainty is not host escape.
  <1>5 [req] Apply also to constant expressions
DLT-5.2-P6
  <1>1 [req] PT5 | `add`/`sub` of a value with pointer atoms and an `INT` set | computes address bits modulo 2^W at the integer operation’s width W, never unbounded offset addition.
  <1>2 [req] Relative displacements from the originating base are modular too: zero net displacement represents that base again, including after an inttoptr truncation to P(a).
  <1>3 [req] Use PT2’s represented-address image construction at W bits (full-width arithmetic, no preserved high GEP bits), retaining original object and ROOT provenance.   deps: DLT-5.2-P3.S1 (PT2)
  <1>4 [req] Keep modular displacement alternatives even outside the allocation, and additionally include (EXT, `*`) and non-handle ⊤ when an image may leave it.
  <1>5 [req] Residue classes and `*` take the same finite-width image; an unrepresentable image retains (X, `*`) for each originating X plus (EXT, `*`) and non-handle ⊤.
  <1>6 [req] Other integer operations on pointer atoms use that conservative image.
  <1>7 [req] Widening a pointer-derived integer by zext/sext uses that conservative image too (fixed reference fallback); ptrtoint zero-extension retains its base representation.
  <1>8 [req] Numerical uncertainty does not itself establish host escape (PT2).   deps: DLT-5.2-P3.S1 (PT2)
  <1>9 [req] The rules apply also to constant expressions, before candidate/dispatch domains freeze; on finite `INT` sets, every LLVM integer operation, cast and `icmp` is evaluated elementwise; with x ⊤ and a constant m, `and x, m` gives the submasks of m and `urem x, m` gives {0, …, m−1} (each still subject to K); a range attribute or `!range` metadata removed by N3/N4 is not a bound on materialised execution and MUST NOT restrict any verdict, candidate set, descriptor shape or dispatch domain.   deps: DLT-12.2-P5.S1 (N3), DLT-12.2-P6.S1 (N4), DLT-3.4-P20.S3 (dispatch domain)
  <1>10 [req] Only bounds independently established by materialised instructions restrict the set; otherwise retain ⊤ and apply the ordinary operation rules, including finite masks/remainders
DLT-5.2-P7
  <1>1 [req] PT6 | `load T, ptr p` | for each (X,o) ∈ AV(p): memory atoms carry their storage interval and representation width; copy a whole-value atom only for that identical interval with a compatible representation.
  <1>2 [req] A known immutable byte image decodes exactly the accessed bytes using DataLayout and T (including initialisers).
  <1>3 [req] For a partial, spanning or overlapping access whose result bits are not represented exactly, the non-handle value is ⊤, never the union of component INT values.
  <1>4 [req] X=EXT gives ⊤.
  <1>5 [req] A non-handle top flag on p contributes the same unknown-address load alternative even when explicit object offsets overlap no known slot; it MUST NOT be dropped.   deps: DLT-2-P10.S1 (slot)
  <1>6 [req] ROOT provenance remains explicit and §6.2's partial-handle restrictions still apply.   deps: DLT-6.2
  <1>7 [req] For a possibly valid load wholly contained in a zero-filled initial extent, include the all-zero value of the load’s representation and width, unioned with values from every overlapping store or copy under these interval rules.
  <1>8 [req] PT8 propagates these initial byte possibilities when copying memory.   deps: DLT-5.2-P9.S1 (PT8)
  <1>9 [req] Zero contributes no ROOT.
  <1>10 [req] Region inputs, replayed caller bytes and other nonzero-initialised contents retain their specified sources; this rule does not replace them with zeros
DLT-5.2-P8
  <1>1 [req] PT7 | `store v, ptr p` | retain each written interval and representation width; partial writes overlapping a larger load participate in PT6's conservative fallback.   deps: DLT-5.2-P7.S1 (PT6)
  <1>2 [req] AV(X, o + d_k) ⊇ AV(v_k) for each (X, o) ∈ AV(p) and each lane or field k at byte offset d_k
DLT-5.2-P9
````

### §5.3 Value sets   [DLT-5.3]

````text
DLT-5.3-P1
  <1>1 [req] The **value set** VS(v) of an integer or pointer operand is the set of its `INT` and `FN` atoms (pointer atoms denote addresses that are not compile-time constants and make VS(v) = ⊤ for dispatch purposes), or ⊤.   deps: DLT-2-P10.S1 (value set)
  <1>2 [req] A value set is a precision tool only:   deps: DLT-2-P10.S1 (value set)
DLT-5.3-P2
  <1>1 [req] an operand with a finite VS is dispatched over it (§3.4, §14.2);   deps: DLT-3.4, DLT-14.2
DLT-5.3-P3
  <1>1 [req] an operand with VS = ⊤ is dispatched over its type's whole valid domain where that domain is finite: operation codes and classes (§3.4), binding kinds (§8.4), the function addresses of a type (§7.2, §14.2);   deps: DLT-4.4-P1.S1 (function address), DLT-3.4, DLT-8.4, DLT-7.2, DLT-14.2
DLT-5.3-P4
  <1>1 [req] otherwise it is a blocker case of §25.1: widths (BLK-1), budgets computed on the device (BLK-2), parameters of in-place pairs (§8.7).   deps: DLT-25.1-P2.S1 (BLK-1), DLT-25.1-P3.S1 (BLK-2), DLT-25.1, DLT-8.7
````

### §6.1 Representation   [DLT-6.1]

````text
DLT-6.1-P1
  <1>1 [req] A handle is an ordinary `ptr` in address space 0.
  <1>2 [req] In device memory and in integers a handle is its **register tag**: an opaque value below 2^pw assigned to an allocation generation (§6.5), nonzero and distinct from every identity still observable through live or stale copies.   deps: DLT-6.5
  <1>3 [req] Physical slots are reusable storage, never allocation identity.   deps: DLT-2-P10.S1 (slot)
  <1>4 [req] A tag MUST NOT be recycled while an observable stale copy can remain; integer wrap is not permission to alias generations.
  <1>5 [req] Copies continue to denote their original generation after free.
  <1>6 [req] ISA 0.8 has no instruction that reads a `qreg`'s launch id (BLK-1's `qreg.id` would add one), so tags are the plugin's.   deps: DLT-25.1-P2.S1 (BLK-1)
  <1>7 [req] At the host–device boundary a handle is the ISA launch register id (`bennett_qreg`, ISA §10), which the launch binds to a `qreg` parameter or result (§6.6).   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register), ISA-10, DLT-6.6
  <1>8 [req] Neither value may influence a result other than through §6.3; the rules below make them unobservable.   deps: DLT-6.3
  <1>9 [req] A handle denotes a register of n wires, n the `qalloc` operand; wire i of handle h is written h.i.   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register), DLT-2-P3.S2 (wire)
````

````text

  <1>1 [req] The **provenance** of a value is the set of `ROOT` atoms of its abstract value (§5).   deps: DLT-5.1-P12.S1 (abstract value), DLT-5

  <1>3 [req] A handle-derived value (any lane or field) MAY be:
DLT-6.2-P2
  <1>1 [req] a handle operand of a marker (§3.2);   deps: DLT-3.2
DLT-6.2-P3
  <1>1 [req] copied by the rules above, including storage in any slot the analysis tracks (§6.4);   deps: DLT-2-P10.S1 (slot), DLT-6.4
DLT-6.2-P4
  <1>1 [req] an operand of `icmp eq` or `icmp ne` (§6.3);   deps: DLT-6.3
DLT-6.2-P5
  <1>1 [req] an argument of a direct or indirect call of a defined function, or a return value.
DLT-6.2-P6
  <1>1 [req] Every other use is `BD-E-HANDLE-USE` (maintainer decision 2: "any other use of a handle-derived integer is rejected fail-loud"; NS §3.1 "never dereferenced"): in particular arithmetic, bitwise operations, `icmp` with any other predicate, any cast other than the copies above (`trunc`, `zext`, `sext`, `bitcast` to a non-pointer-width type, `ptrtoint` to a width ≠ pw), `getelementptr` with a handle as base or index, `switch` on it, use as the pointer operand of a `load`, `store`, `atomicrmw`, `cmpxchg` or memory intrinsic (dereference), and a load of any type whose byte range overlaps a handle-derived slot without being exactly one pw-wide lane of it (a partial read).   deps: DLT-22.1-P11.S1 (BD-E-HANDLE-USE), DLT-2-P10.S1 (slot)
DLT-6.2-P7

  <1>2 [non] *(non-normative)* A tracked value that at run time is not a live handle (a stale copy, a freed register) traps at the marker (`T-DEAD`, §18.3).   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register), DLT-18.3
DLT-6.2-P8
  <1>1 [req] Dynamically indexed handle vectors MUST use PT10 lane provenance and N15 total index semantics, retaining explicit ROOT atoms and adding zero only for possible out-of-range extraction.   deps: DLT-5.2-P11.S1 (PT10), DLT-12.2-P17.S1 (N15)   declared: DLT-5.2-P11, DLT-6.2-P1, DLT-12.2-P17, ISA-4.1, ISA-4.2
````

### §6.3 Comparison (maintainer decision 4)   [DLT-6.3]

````text
DLT-6.3-P1
  <1>1 [req] `icmp eq` and `icmp ne` of a handle with `null`, or with another handle-derived value, compare **identity**: a live handle is never null, and two handles are equal iff they denote the same allocation generation, including when comparing a freed identity with a later allocation in the same physical slot.   deps: DLT-2-P10.S1 (slot)
  <1>2 [req] The result is not handle-derived.
  <1>3 [req] In CC it lowers to `icmp` on register tags.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC), DLT-6.1-P1.S2 (register tag)
  <1>4 [req] This covers C `if (!q)` and Rust's `Option<Handle>` niche (audit D8).   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (Handle)
  <1>5 [non] *(non-normative)* A comparison is a classical observation of identity, not of the register's content; ids are unique, so it equals the native comparison of the two handle values.   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register)
DLT-6.3-P2
  <1>1 [req] Handle equality and null tests MUST compare allocation identity, preserve stale-versus-new inequality and produce a result without handle provenance.   deps: ~DLT-2-P3.S1 (Handle)   declared: DLT-6.1-P1, DLT-6.3-P1, ISA-3.3-P7, ISA-4.1-P4
````

````text
DLT-6.4-P5
````

### §6.5 Realisation on ISA 0.8: static register files   [DLT-6.5]

````text
DLT-6.5-P1
  <1>1 [req] ISA 0.8 has no instruction that stores, loads or converts a `qreg` (ISA §3.2, §3.3, §4.1), and `qreg[n]` types have literal widths.   deps: ISA-3.2, ISA-3.3, ISA-4.1
  <1>2 [req] CC code holds `qreg` values in its classical environment (dynamic SSA instances, block parameters, call arguments and results; ISA §3.2, §7.4).   deps: DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC), ISA-3.2, ISA-7.4
  <1>3 [req] The plugin realises each allocation site s (a `qalloc` or `qborrow` call) in one of two ways:   deps: DLT-5.1-P4.S1 (allocation site)
DLT-6.5-P2
  <1>1 [req] **Direct.** If no `ROOT(s)` atom reaches a memory slot (PT7, PT8), the handle is a CC `qreg` value threaded through SSA values, block parameters, call arguments and results ("register- environment passing"; §25.2 records that ISA §3.3's transition table should name CC `call`, `ret` and `br` operands of `qreg` type).   deps: DLT-5.2-P8.S1 (PT7), DLT-5.2-P9.S1 (PT8), DLT-2-P10.S1 (slot), DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC), DLT-25.2, ISA-3.3
  <1>2 [req] Every execution of s creates a new dynamic instance, so loops and recursion need no bound.
DLT-6.5-P3
  <1>1 [req] **Static register file.** Otherwise a physical **slot** is a pair (s, instance index k < N(s)); ROOT(s) is static provenance, not run-time identity.   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register), DLT-2-P10.S1 (slot)
  <1>2 [req] For each slot the plugin keeps one CC `qreg` variable, threaded like a direct handle through every CC variant that may use it; `qalloc` at s picks a free instance index at run time and executes `qreg.new cls n` into that variable (one variable per member of the width dispatch domain, §3.4).   deps: DLT-2-P10.S1 (slot), DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC), DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant), DLT-3.4-P20.S3 (dispatch domain), DLT-3.4
  <1>3 [req] The default CC table holds each slot's current generation tag and liveness; a fresh-tag allocator gives every allocation a new identity (§6.1), stored in memory.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC), DLT-2-P10.S1 (slot), DLT-6.1
  <1>4 [req] A marker operand is dispatched by matching its full tag against current live candidate slots (compare tree, §14.2); a missing or retired generation traps T-DEAD before changing any register.   deps: DLT-2-P10.S1 (slot), DLT-2-P3.S1 (register), DLT-14.2
  <1>5 [req] Free retires the identity even if the slot is immediately reused.   deps: DLT-2-P10.S1 (slot)
  <1>6 [req] Recycle tags only after old copies are proven unobservable, never by slot reuse alone.   deps: DLT-2-P10.S1 (slot)
  <1>7 [req] This table and allocator use ordinary classical operations, without qreg.id.
  <1>8 [req] N(s) bounds simultaneous physical slots, not the number of historical identities.   deps: DLT-2-P10.S1 (slot)
  <1>9 [req] A direct handle that is converted to an integer (`ptrtoint`, a store) gets a tag in the same way.
DLT-6.5-P4
  <1>1 [def] **Reference instance bound** of a site s in function F with a static register file:   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register)
DLT-6.5-P5
  <1>1 [req] Before rules 1–2, augment each function's CFG with N29 continuation edges: from every call whose closure may longjmp, add an edge to each setjmp continuation in every function that may be an ancestor of that call (including the same function).   deps: DLT-12.2-P31.S1 (N29)
  <1>2 [req] Include the materialised __bennett_rt_setjmp continuations, candidate callees and interprocedural call edges.
  <1>3 [req] The reference default remains conservative: if a setjmp continuation in any may-ancestor A of F (A=F included) can reach s through these CFG and call edges, s is not self-disjoint and E(s)=∞.   deps: DLT-6.5-P8.S1 (self-disjoint)
  <1>4 [req] Apply this rule to §7.5(b) R hoisting as well.   deps: DLT-7.5-P3
  <1>5 [req] Such a site uses BLK-1 (R hoisting: BLK-4), with the bounded static-file fallback, never rejection.   deps: DLT-25.1-P2.S1 (BLK-1), DLT-25.1-P5.S1 (BLK-4)
  <1>6 [req] The read-only ISA 0.9 draft's K1 supplies the exact missing dynamic qreg.width/id/from_id and run-time-width register capability; K2 supplies R allocation for BLK-4.   deps: DLT-25.1-P5.S1 (BLK-4), DLT-2-P3.S1 (register)

DLT-6.5-P6

  <1>2 [req] Use BLK-1, with the bounded static-file fallback, never rejection.   deps: DLT-25.1-P2.S1 (BLK-1)
  <1>3 [req] The host may call entries any number of times: executions per entry call do not bound instances that survive return.
  <1>4 [req] Under §7.5(b), substitute reversible-invocation return and BLK-4; the same boundary test precedes hoisting.   deps: DLT-25.1-P5.S1 (BLK-4), DLT-7.5-P3
  <1>5 [req] An internal callee's return alone is not a device-entry return: a guaranteed free in its caller before the entry returns can discharge this condition.

  <1>6 [req] A handle parameter used directly only within its receiving entry keeps the direct realisation, as does a returned QREG never stored in memory.   deps: DLT-6.6-P1.S2 (handle parameter)
  <1>7 [req] The infinite bound on a returned root is relevant to its static-file realisation when it reaches memory; it does not impose a finite bound on direct QREG transport.
  <1>8 [req] Under §7.5(b), substitute reversible-invocation exit and BLK-4 (`blocked:BD-B-ISA12`) for receipt through env.   deps: DLT-25.1-P5.S1 (BLK-4), DLT-7.5-P3
DLT-6.5-P8

  <1>2 [def] Then N(s) = 1.
DLT-6.5-P9
````

### §6.6 Host–device boundary   [DLT-6.6]

````text
DLT-6.6-P1
  <1>1 [unc] A device entry's parameters and results of handle type bind to launch `QREG` arguments and results (ISA §10).   deps: ISA-10
  <1>2 [def] A `ptr` parameter of a device entry is a **handle parameter** iff its candidate atom `ROOT(E, i)` (added by PT11 to every pointer parameter of every device entry) reaches a marker handle operand; otherwise the candidate atom is removed before §6.2 is checked.   deps: DLT-5.2-P12.S1 (PT11), DLT-6.2
  <1>3 [req] A handle parameter binds to `QREG`; host code may copy, store and compare launch register ids and pass them back.   deps: DLT-6.6-P1.S2 (handle parameter), DLT-2-P3.S1 (register)
  <1>4 [req] Leak checking happens at program end and at `bennett_qreg_free`, not at each device-entry return, which gives the REPL's lexical lifetime (NS §5; audit B-30).
  <1>5 [non] *(non-normative)* A register returned to the host stays live across launches until the host frees it or a `measure` consumes it (ISA §10: "register ids created by the run remain valid unless measured or freed").   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register), ISA-10
````

````text
DLT-6.8-P1
  <1>1 [req] The plugin converts handles to ISA wires (ISA §3.3 linear values) when it lowers.   deps: DLT-2-P3.S2 (wire), ISA-3.3
````

### §7.2 Candidate sets and dispatch (maintainer decision 3)   [DLT-7.2]

````text
DLT-7.2-P1
  <1>1 [req] The candidate set RR(v) of a region operand v is computed from its abstract value (§5):   deps: DLT-5.1-P12.S1 (abstract value), DLT-5
DLT-7.2-P2
  <1>1 [req] every `FN(F)` atom of AV(v), resolved by `resolve` below;
DLT-7.2-P3
  <1>1 [req] if AV(v) has the ⊤ flag: in addition every function of the required type of §7.1 (for `oracle`/`inplace`: every function) whose address is used anywhere in the linked program, resolved (decision 3 read literally: "every function whose address can reach a region marker"; audit B-33).   deps: DLT-7.1
  <1>2 [req] The set is therefore always bounded by the program.
DLT-7.2-P4
  <1>1 [req] `resolve(F)` follows aliases to their aliasee and **forwarding thunks** to their target: F is a forwarding thunk of G iff F's body is one block holding exactly a call of G (optionally `tail`/`musttail`/`notail`, default calling convention, no operand bundles) whose arguments are F's parameters in order and whose function type equals F's, followed by `ret void` or `ret` of that call's result; then `resolve(F) = resolve(G)`, except that a thunk on a cycle of thunks resolves to itself (it is an ordinary defined function whose execution recurses until a budget or the host stops it; 0.1's `BD-E-REGION-THUNK` is deleted).
DLT-7.2-P5
  <1>1 [req] **Dispatch.** The region operand is classical data.
  <1>2 [req] The plugin compiles a body for every candidate.
  <1>3 [req] At run time the operand's value is compared, by the compare tree of §14.2 over the sorted keys, with A(S) of every **source** S (every function or alias that resolves into the candidate set and whose address reaches v, plus every candidate itself); on equality the region `resolve(S)` is entered.   deps: DLT-14.2
  <1>4 [req] No match is the run-time trap `T-REGION` (fault code 4).
  <1>5 [req] A candidate with no definition (an external declaration, a function without bitcode) is entered as a trapped call: F(8) with a coverage line (§4.5 item 4).   deps: DLT-2-P15.S1 (trapped), DLT-4.5-P5
DLT-7.2-P6
  <1>1 [req] **Ill-formed candidates.** A candidate that is not well-formed for the marker's kind (a type other than §7.1's, or a violation of §7.5) is compiled as a **trap body** (`T-REGION-INVALID`, fault code 4) with a coverage line: it may never be dispatched, so it is not a compile-time error.   deps: DLT-7.1, DLT-7.5
  <1>2 [req] It is rejected (`BD-E-REGION-TYPE`, `BD-E-REGION-MEASURE`, `BD-E-REVERSIBLE-MEASURE`) only when it is the **unique** candidate, because then every execution of the marker fails (outline E14).   deps: DLT-22.1-P14.S1 (BD-E-REGION-TYPE), DLT-22.1-P15.S1 (BD-E-REGION-MEASURE), DLT-22.1-P16.S1 (BD-E-REVERSIBLE-MEASURE)
DLT-7.2-P7
  <1>1 [req] 0.1's `BD-E-REGION-UNBOUNDED` and `BD-E-REGION-EXTERNAL` are deleted.
DLT-7.2-P8
  <1>1 [req] Region operands loaded from tracked memory or relative tables MUST use the reference candidate analysis and its type-compatible address-taken fallback, with no blanket TOP rejection.   deps: ~DLT-2-P5.S2 (Region operand)   declared: DLT-5.2, DLT-7.2, DLT-12.8-P10, ISA-4.1, ISA-4.2, ISA-9.2
````

### §7.3 Region identity (maintainer decision 1)   [DLT-7.3]

````text
DLT-7.3-P1
  <1>1 [req] A region is identified by its content, never by its symbol.
  <1>2 [req] Candidates that resolve to the same function are one region.
  <1>3 [req] The semantic identity of an **oracle region** in a shape (§8.4) is the interface hash (ISA §9.2) of `@ref` in its reference object (§16.2): every lproc, data image and layout leaf of the closure is part of it, and `@ref`, `@L<n>`, `@G<n>` are fixed names, so two functions with equal materialised bodies have equal identity whatever their source names.   deps: DLT-16-P1.S1 (reference object), DLT-8.4, ISA-9.2, DLT-16.2
  <1>4 [req] Symbol names, linkage, aliases and thunks are non-normative: diagnostics and coverage entries MAY print them.
  <1>5 [req] Budget lookup uses the separate provisional `selection_identity` and the once-only staging of §9.2, never a fixed point in this final semantic identity.   deps: DLT-9.2-P3.S2 (selection_identity), DLT-9.2
DLT-7.3-P2
  <1>1 [def] The **region key** of any region is the SHA-256 of the text printed by the LLVM printer of the major in use for a module that contains the materialised region function and its closure, after `strip` (local names), with the functions renamed `f0, f1, …` in depth-first preorder from the region along direct calls in instruction order, and without datalayout, triple and module metadata.
  <1>2 [req] It keys the budget table (§9.2) and is recorded in the certificate and coverage entries.   deps: DLT-9.2-P2.S1 (budget table), DLT-9.2
  <1>3 [req] It depends on the LLVM major, which the certificate records (§24, D13).   deps: DLT-24-P3.S1 (D13), DLT-24
````
