### §7.5 Static well-formedness   [DLT-7.5]

````text
DLT-7.5-P1
  <1>1 [req] Only the rules the north star requires:
DLT-7.5-P2
  <1>1 [req] **(a) Measurement in a unitary region.** A `measure` call in the closure of an action region is `BD-E-REGION-MEASURE` (NS §3.1: "user measurement inside it is refused"), unless the module requests **deferred measurement** with the module flag `!{i32 1, !"bennett.measure_in_unitary", !"defer"}` (NS §3.1: "or, when the front end asks for it, deferred by the deferred-measurement principle, which the certificate states").   deps: DLT-22.1-P15.S1 (BD-E-REGION-MEASURE), DLT-7.1-P7.S3 (action region)
  <1>2 [req] Then a `measure(h, i)` inside a generation becomes a `qcopy` of `h.i` onto a fresh wire w (ISA §4.5), the call's `i1` result is a Co value whose wire is w (§10, TDL-2 seed).   deps: DLT-10-P3.S1 (TDL-2), DLT-2-P3.S2 (wire), ISA-4.5, DLT-10
  <1>3 [req] Retain this intentional outcome record until the first permitted CC measurement boundary after the outermost action returns, and measure it there before the next source operation.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC)
  <1>4 [req] Earlier removal requires the complete instrument (outcomes and correlations included) to be unchanged; an open window alone never justifies quncopy.
  <1>5 [req] These channel outputs are separate from clean workspace (TDL-7).   deps: DLT-10-P35.S1 (TDL-7)
  <1>6 [req] Standalone adj uses the deterministic latest-before-reversed-consumer placement of §18.2, including source-wire lifetime extension.   deps: DLT-18.2
  <1>7 [req] The coverage report has a `lowered` entry with source `dialect-0.2.11:7.5a` for every such call, and the certificate lists the id `deferred_measurement` in the region's `definedness_assumptions` (ISA §12.3; §25.2 records the wording item).   deps: ~DLT-2-P15.S1 (lowered), ~ISA-12.3, DLT-25.2   declared: DLT-7.5, DLT-19.9, DLT-25.2
DLT-7.5-P3
  <1>1 [req] **(b) Reversible regions.** The closure of a reversible region MAY contain gate and region markers on handles received through `env`: they lower to R-tier `action_call`/`oracle_call` (ISA §3.1, §4.7), recorded in the R history and reversed by re-application or adjoint (ISA §7.4).   deps: DLT-2-P6.S3 (Reversible region), ISA-3.1, ISA-4.7, ISA-7.4
  <1>2 [req] A `measure` call in the closure is `BD-E-REVERSIBLE-MEASURE` (ISA §10: a run that measured is not reversible; ISA §3.3: a `measure` frame is never reversed).   deps: DLT-22.1-P16.S1 (BD-E-REVERSIBLE-MEASURE), ISA-10, ISA-3.3
  <1>3 [req] A `qalloc`, `qborrow` or `qfree` in the closure is **hoisted** (ISA 0.8 has `qreg.new` in CC only): when every such site s has a finite reference instance bound N(s) (§6.5 rules 1 and 2, applied to every site whether or not it reaches memory, including the entry-boundary liveness precondition with the reversible invocation in place of the device entry), the CC caller allocates N(s) clean registers per site before the R call, passes them as `qreg` arguments, and frees them after it returns; `qalloc` in R selects a free one, `qfree` checks that it is clean (`T-CLEAN`) and returns it to the free set.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC), DLT-2-P3.S1 (register), DLT-6.5-P8, DLT-6.5-P9
  <1>4 [req] Otherwise the site is a blocker point of BLK-4 (`blocked:BD-B-ISA12`, §25.1).   deps: DLT-25.1-P5.S1 (BLK-4), DLT-6.5-P10.S1 (blocker point), DLT-25.1
DLT-7.5-P4
  <1>1 [req] **(c) In-place pairs** are verified by §8.7.   deps: DLT-8.7
DLT-7.5-P5
  <1>1 [req] Deferred measurement is a channel on adjoint paths as well: the special §18.2 rule creates fresh retained records for standalone adj and retains E_f records through compute.   deps: DLT-18.2
  <1>2 [req] An open window never authorises quncopy of these records.
DLT-7.5-P6
  <1>1 [req] Front-end-requested deferred measurement MUST retain its channel records through the declared observation boundary, including the accepted standalone-adjoint and compute placement rules.   deps: DLT-7.5-P2.S1 (deferred measurement)   declared: DLT-7.5, DLT-18.2, ISA-4.4, ISA-4.6, ISA-12.1
````

### §7.6 Outlining conventions   [DLT-7.6]

````text
DLT-7.6-P1
  <1>1 [req] Regions are functions on arrival: the front end outlines (a Julia macro, a clang attribute, a Rust closure trampoline); the dialect imposes no source syntax.
  <1>2 [req] The plugin additionally outlines coherent slices (TDL-3), which is not observable beyond §18.   deps: DLT-10-P14.S1 (TDL-3), DLT-18
DLT-7.6-P2
  <1>1 [req] Action and reversible regions have type `void (ptr env)`.
  <1>2 [req] `env` points to classical memory the front end owns (an `alloca` or heap object) that is live for the duration of the marker call; the region reads and writes it as classical memory (§18.4).   deps: DLT-3.5-P1.S1 (marker call), DLT-18.4
  <1>3 [req] Handles reach a region through `env` (PT9 binds a region's parameter to the marker's env argument).   deps: DLT-5.2-P10.S1 (PT9), DLT-2-P3.S1 (Handle)
DLT-7.6-P3
  <1>1 [req] Oracle regions are arbitrary functions bound by a descriptor (§8); no packing wrapper is needed (audit D21).   deps: DLT-2-P6.S2 (Oracle region), DLT-8
DLT-7.6-P4
  <1>1 [req] A region body MUST be referenced by the region operand (directly or through §7.2); a body referenced only from a side-table global is not a region (enzyme survey implication 5).   deps: DLT-7.2
DLT-7.6-P5
  <1>1 [req] Region functions SHOULD have internal linkage, so that they are not device entries.   deps: DLT-3.8-P3.S1 (Region functions)
  <1>2 [req] C++ lambdas pass their static `__invoke` thunk and Rust closures an `extern "C"` trampoline; both are ordinary region functions whose closure contains the closure body.
````

### §8 The oracle interface (oracle-abi 0.2.4)   [DLT-8]

````text
DLT-8-P1
  <1>1 [req] `__bennett_oracle(f, budget, desc)` applies the lifted oracle of region function f, under the budget of §9, to the registers and classical values that the **descriptor** `desc` binds to f's parameters, result and device models.   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register), DLT-9
  <1>2 [req] `__bennett_inplace(g, ginv, budget, desc)` applies an in-place bijection (§8.7).   deps: DLT-8.7
  <1>3 [req] The descriptor is classical data in the caller's memory, built by plain stores (§3.8); its kinds are classical values dispatched over their finite domains (§8.4).   deps: DLT-3.8, DLT-8.4
````

### §8.1 Descriptor layout   [DLT-8.1]

````text
DLT-8.1-P1
  <1>1 [req] The descriptor is the LLVM struct `{ H, [nparam x Bind], [ndev x DevBind] }` laid out by the module's datalayout, where (C view in `bennett_markers.h`, §3.3):   deps: DLT-3.3
DLT-8.1-P2
  <1>1 [req] H | `{ i32, i32, i32, i32, ptr, ptr }` | `version` (= 2), `nparam`, `ndev`, `flags` (= 0), `tgt`, `fault`
DLT-8.1-P3
  <1>1 [req] Bind | `{ i32, i32, ptr, i64, i64 }` | `kind`, `mode`, `q`, `value`, `size`
DLT-8.1-P4
  <1>1 [req] DevBind | `{ i32, i32, ptr, i64 }` | `model`, `mode` (= 0), `q`, `value`
DLT-8.1-P5
  <1>1 [req] On x86-64, AArch64 and RISC-V64 (pw = 64) H is 32 bytes, Bind 32 bytes (`kind` at 0, `mode` 4, `q` 8, `value` 16, `size` 24) and DevBind 24 bytes, so `param[i]` is at 32 + 32i and `dev[j]` at 32 + 32·nparam + 24j.
  <1>2 [req] The plugin reads the descriptor at the marker call, in the caller's tier, with ordinary loads.   deps: DLT-3.5-P1.S1 (marker call)
  <1>3 [req] `nparam` MUST equal the number of flattened scalar fields of the dispatched region function after N21/N22 and ABI lowering, using §8.2 carriers (one field for a scalar).   deps: DLT-12.2-P23.S1 (N21), DLT-12.2-P24.S1 (N22), DLT-8.2
  <1>4 [req] A descriptor whose `version`, `flags`, `nparam` or any kind, mode or model is not one this section defines, or whose binding does not fit the parameter's type (below), traps (`T-IFACE`, fault code 4) when the marker is called.
````

### §8.2 Parameter bindings   [DLT-8.2]

````text
DLT-8.2-P1
  <1>1 [req] Let the dispatched region function have IR parameters p_0 … p_{m−1} and return type R (`void` or a first-class type of at most 128 payload bits after N25, §12.2).   deps: DLT-12.2-P27.S1 (N25), DLT-12.2
  <1>2 [req] Before binding, represent each floating-point scalar by its §13.1 integer carrier (half/bfloat i16, float i32, double i64, x86_fp80 i80, fp128/ppc_fp128 i128).   deps: DLT-13.1
  <1>3 [req] IN and ARG bind carrier bits.
  <1>4 [req] Flatten aggregate/vector parameters depth-first in field/lane order, one Bind per scalar field; apply N21/N22 first.   deps: DLT-12.2-P23.S1 (N21), DLT-12.2-P24.S1 (N22)
  <1>5 [req] `param[i]` binds flattened field i.
  <1>6 [req] Results concatenate fields in the same order, field 0 in the lowest bits, no padding; width is the sum of scalar carrier widths.
  <1>7 [req] N25 demotes results whose packed width exceeds 128 bits.   deps: DLT-12.2-P27.S1 (N25)
  <1>8 [req] Memory accesses retain datalayout padding; this padding is never part of the packed return payload:
DLT-8.2-P2
  <1>1 [req] `IN` | 1 | `iW` or `ptr addrspace(a)` (W = P(a)) | q with n(q) ≤ W | the parameter's value is the basis value of q, zero-extended (`mode` = ZEXT 0) or sign-extended (`mode` = SEXT 1) to W; a `ptr` parameter may be `IN` (a superposed pointer) | an `ins` bundle `x<k>:wire[n(q)]` (a pseudo-location, ISA §3.7), extended by `lift.zext`/`lift.sext` in the wrapper   deps: DLT-2-P3.S2 (wire), ISA-3.7
DLT-8.2-P3
  <1>1 [req] `ARG` | 2 | `iW` (W ≤ 128) or `ptr` | none (`q` ignored) | a classical value: bits 0–63 from `value`, bits 64–127 from `size`; a `ptr` ARG is an address in the caller's classical memory, which the oracle reads through its entry state (§8.5) | an `args` entry `a<k>:i<W>` (W = P(a) for `ptr addrspace(a)`; ISA §4.7, §5.1)   deps: DLT-8.5, ISA-4.7, ISA-5.1
DLT-8.2-P4
  <1>1 [req] `MEM_IN` | 3 | `ptr` | q with n(q) = 8·2^A, `size` = 2^A | the parameter is the base address of an interface region of 2^A bytes whose cell i is byte i of q (bits [8i, 8i + 8)); its contents may be superposed; role `in` (restored on every basis configuration, ISA §5.1).   deps: ISA-5.1
  <1>2 [req] This is the quantum-addressed memory of NS §8 rung 4 | a `mem` region `m<k>:region[A,8] in`; the argument is `lift.addr @m<k>`
DLT-8.2-P5
  <1>1 [req] `OUT` | 4 | `ptr` | q with n(q) = 8·`size` | the parameter points to a fresh zero-filled buffer of `size` bytes in the oracle's memory; at exit its final bytes are XORed into q, byte k into wires [8k, 8k + 8) (a declared output, NS §4.2) | `lift.alloc size` in the wrapper; the bytes are part of the payload (§8.6)   deps: DLT-2-P3.S2 (wire), DLT-8.6
DLT-8.2-P6
  <1>1 [req] `INOUT` | 5 | `iW` | q with n(q) = W | `inplace` only (§8.7): the in-place register x | `qinplace … x`   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register), DLT-8.7
DLT-8.2-P7
  <1>1 [req] The **result**: a non-null `tgt` register receives the return value: payload bits = the return value zero-extended to n(tgt) if n(tgt) ≥ R's width; if n(tgt) is narrower, the dropped bits are checked and an execution on which they are nonzero faults with code 4 (`FAULT_UB_TRAP`); the retained bits are the low n(tgt).   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register)
  <1>2 [req] A null `tgt` discards the return value.
  <1>3 [req] For `oracle`, the **fault register** `fault` MUST be a register of exactly 4 wires (ISA §5.4: F = 4) and MUST NOT be null (`T-IFACE`).   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register), DLT-2-P3.S2 (wire), ISA-5.4
  <1>4 [req] Null `tgt` remains valid for a `void` function or a discarded non-void return.
  <1>5 [req] If there is no `OUT` or non-null `CONSOLE` output either, the shape has zero payload outputs; it still executes once and delivers its fault through §8.6's synthetic variant.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant), DLT-8.6
  <1>6 [req] Every register named by the descriptor MUST be live and pairwise distinct (`T-DEAD`, `T-ALIAS`).   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register)
  <1>7 [req] A width mismatch in the table above is `T-SIZE`.
````

### §8.3 Device bindings   [DLT-8.3]

````text
DLT-8.3-P1
  <1>1 [unc] `dev[j]` binds a device model for the lifted (coherent) tier (§11.3):   deps: DLT-11.3
DLT-8.3-P2
  <1>1 [req] `ENTROPY` | 1 | q with n(q) = 8·2^A | an `in` region `e0:region[A,8]` holding the entropy tape, possibly superposed (NS §8 rung 8: "the entropy device is replaced by a superposed register")   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register)
DLT-8.3-P3

DLT-8.3-P4

DLT-8.3-P5

DLT-8.3-P6
  <1>1 [unc] At most one binding per model.
  <1>2 [req] A model without a binding is **unbound**: an effect on it in L code faults with code 8 on the executions that reach it (§11.3; NS §4.2).   deps: DLT-11.3
````

### §8.4 Shapes and dispatch   [DLT-8.4]

````text
DLT-8.4-P1
  <1>1 [req] A **shape** is the tuple (region candidate F; for each parameter its kind, mode, register width n(q) and `size`; n(tgt) or "none"; for each device binding its model and n(q)).   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register)
  <1>2 [req] The kind, mode, model, `size` and `value` fields have value sets (§5.3); register widths come from the register file (§6.5), whose roots have known widths.   deps: DLT-2-P10.S1 (value set), DLT-2-P3.S1 (register), DLT-5.3, DLT-6.5
  <1>3 [req] The plugin compiles one reference object (§16.2) per shape that the value sets allow, taking every unbounded kind or mode field over its finite domain (5 kinds, 2 modes, 4 models), so the number of shapes is always bounded.   deps: DLT-16-P1.S1 (reference object), DLT-2-P10.S1 (value set), DLT-16.2
  <1>4 [req] At run time the caller's tier reads the descriptor and selects the compiled shape with the compare tree of §14.2; a descriptor that matches no compiled shape traps (`T-IFACE`), which happens only for a field outside its table.   deps: DLT-14.2
  <1>5 [req] `value` and `size` of `ARG` bindings are the oracle's classical arguments and are not part of the shape.
  <1>6 [non] *(non-normative)* With one valid value per shape field there is one shape per candidate.
  <1>7 [req] Initial zero possibilities still participate in §5; kind 0 is outside the five-kind table and takes T-IFACE rather than creating an additional valid shape.   deps: DLT-5
DLT-8.4-P2
  <1>1 [req] The marker then issues, in the caller's tier, one **oracle invocation** (§8.6) whose operands are the static registers the descriptor's handles denote (§6.5), the budget token (§9.5) and the classical arguments.   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register), DLT-8.6, DLT-6.5, DLT-9.5
DLT-8.4-P3
  <1>1 [req] ARG bindings MUST carry the caller's fixed-at-entry values in parameter order without specialising their values into the shape, and pointer arguments MUST retain entry-state semantics.   declared: DLT-8.2-P3, DLT-8.4-P1, DLT-8.5, ISA-4.7-P1, ISA-12.3-P2
````

### §8.5 Entry state   [DLT-8.5]

````text
DLT-8.5-P1
  <1>1 [req] **Reference semantics.** The region function runs on a **private copy of the caller's whole classical memory at the call**, with the bound inputs; its writes are discarded except through `OUT`, `tgt` and the bound device outputs (NS §4.2: "every other write being restored workspace").
  <1>2 [req] Constant globals, and mutable globals that only the oracle's own L closure writes, equal their initialisers at every call.
DLT-8.5-P2
  <1>1 [req] **Realisation on ISA 0.8.** Let R be the abstract objects the oracle closure may load (§5.4), minus constant globals and mutable globals written by no function outside the L closure.   deps: DLT-5.1-P1.S1 (abstract objects), DLT-5.4
  <1>2 [req] Translate source read-set objects after normalisation to runtime backing allocations.
  <1>3 [req] If R includes a caller alloca/frame, include its live shadow-stack backing storage and metadata, bytes and addresses.
  <1>4 [req] If reachability is uncertain, include all live caller heap/stack backing allocations.
  <1>5 [req] Whenever the L closure uses the shadow stack, add its state globals to G and its block to Hb with current base, size and stack pointer, even without a source heap object.
  <1>6 [req] Include the logical frame/allocation table of §17.3, dynamic extents, liveness and save/restore state in G whenever stack access or stack operations can execute.   deps: DLT-17.3
  <1>7 [req] Replay these bytes before private allocations/accesses and let ss_init adopt them; a live backing entry alone does not recreate live program frames.
  <1>8 [req] All such metadata mutations invalidate snapshot reuse independently of the byte read set.
  <1>9 [req] Allocator metadata is an independent entry-state dependency: allocation, deallocation, allocation-validity checks and observation of allocation-derived addresses read it even without an LLVM load.
  <1>10 [req] Replay the complete caller allocation history (sizes and live bits) whenever any can execute, including when the byte read set R is empty.
  <1>11 [req] Bytes are included only for byte dependencies; the sound default is the complete table, with a smaller proven dependency optional.
  <1>12 [req] Only when both byte and allocator-state dependencies are absent may transfer be omitted and globals start at their images (ISA §3.7), as in rung 4 route A (SQLite §5.2(i)).   deps: ISA-3.7
  <1>13 [req] After replay heap_used, atop and stack-state values equal the caller's call-entry values.
  <1>14 [req] Otherwise the plugin emits an **entry-state transfer**:
DLT-8.5-P3
  <1>1 [req] **Snapshot.** At the call the caller's tier forms the byte string S = k ‖ (size_i ‖ live_i)_{i<k} ‖ G ‖ Hb, where k is an 8-byte little-endian count of heap allocations in the caller's allocation table (in allocation order, ISA §7.1), `size_i` and `live_i` are 8-byte little-endian fields (`live_i` is 0 or 1), G is the bytes of the mutable globals in R in `layout.globals` order, and Hb is the bytes of every live heap allocation in allocation order if R contains a heap object or shadow-stack backing allocation (else empty); each live Hb segment has exactly size_i bytes, even for size_i=0.   deps: ISA-7.1
  <1>2 [req] S is zero-padded to 2^A_s bytes, where A_s is the smallest exponent with 2^A_s ≥ 8 + 16·N_alloc + Σ|G| + `heap_limit_max` (N_alloc the allocation-table capacity of the layout, §19.5); A_s is static.   deps: DLT-19.5
  <1>3 [req] The snapshot bytes S are assembled in a plugin-added unnamed CC global of 2^A_s bytes, zero-filled before every build; thus all 16-byte leaf loads, including padding, are valid.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC)
DLT-8.5-P4
  <1>1 [req] **Register.** The CC tier builds a register of 8·2^A_s wires holding S with a **concat tree** of A_s − 3 static-width CC functions `B_j` (j = 4, …, A_s): `B_4(p)` executes `qreg.new any 128`, loads the 16 bytes at p as two `i64` values and makes the `oracle_call` of the runtime oracle `@xor128` (§16.5) that XORs them into the register (with a token minted at launch for budget (6, 0, 0, 0) and a fresh 4-wire fault register, which stays clean and is freed); `B_j(p)` (j > 4) returns `qreg.concat B_{j−1}(p) B_{j−1}(p + 2^{j−1})`.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC), DLT-2-P3.S1 (register), DLT-2-P3.S2 (wire), DLT-8.2-P7.S3 (fault register), DLT-16.5
  <1>2 [req] Every type is static and the cost is 2^(A_s−4) region calls.
  <1>3 [req] The register is bound as an extra `in` region `s0:region[A_s,8]`.   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register)
DLT-8.5-P5
  <1>1 [req] **Replay.** The wrapper prologue (§16.2) calls the runtimes function `__bennett_rt_entry_replay(s0)`, which for i < k executes `__bennett_nz_alloc(size_i)` (ISA `lift.alloc`) and, if `live_i` = 0, `__bennett_nz_free` of the result.   deps: DLT-16.2
  <1>2 [req] ISA §4.2 `lift.alloc` and ISA §7.1 `alloc` share the rule "bump + max(n, 1) from `heap_base`", so the replay reproduces the caller's heap addresses exactly (audit O-07).   deps: ISA-4.2, ISA-7.1
  <1>3 [req] It then copies G into the globals (by the driver-generated table `__bennett_rt_entry_table` of their addresses and sizes) and Hb into the replayed live allocations.
DLT-8.5-P6
  <1>1 [req] **Release.** The snapshot register holds the basis state |S⟩ and is unentangled after every oracle call (an `in` region is unchanged on every basis configuration, ISA §5.2).   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register), ISA-5.2
  <1>2 [req] The caller keeps it for later calls only while its dependent bytes and allocator metadata are unchanged.
  <1>3 [req] Relevant alloc/free and shadow-stack push/pop/restore invalidate it as well as stores to R, and releases it by unpreparation: retain the classical S for the register's lifetime, take successive slice views of at most 128 bits, invoke the same @xor128 preparation oracle with the original two i64 arguments on each 128-bit chunk (one view per call), then qreg.free the now-clean whole register.   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register)
  <1>4 [req] A_s ≥ 4, so every leaf is exactly 128 bits.
  <1>5 [req] No whole-register measurement, view measurement or un-concat operation is needed.
DLT-8.5-P7
  <1>1 [req] The replay's rows, allocations and calls are part of the reference body and count against the budget (§9.4).   deps: DLT-9.4
  <1>2 [req] Entry-state transfer from R-tier code needs registers allocated in R (BLK-4, §25.1); no rung uses it.   deps: DLT-25.1-P5.S1 (BLK-4), DLT-2-P3.S1 (register), DLT-25.1
  <1>3 [req] **Build-time snapshots** (rung 7, §19.6) rewrite the initialisers of the mutable globals to snapshot values at link time, so byte transfer may be empty; allocator dependencies still require replay.   deps: DLT-19.6
  <1>4 [req] Efficiency: G-12 (§25.3).   deps: DLT-25.3
````

### §8.6 Oracle invocations and wide outputs   [DLT-8.6]

````text
DLT-8.6-P1
  <1>1 [req] The **outputs** of a shape are, in order: `tgt` (if non-null), each `OUT` parameter in parameter order, and the `CONSOLE` register (if bound and non-null).   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register)
  <1>2 [req] Each output register is split into **slices** of at most 128 bits from its low end (ISA §3.3: payloads are `iN` with N ≤ 128); the slices of all outputs are numbered 0, 1, …, k − 1 in that order.   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register), ISA-3.3
  <1>3 [req] Every slice j has an oracle **variant** W_j: the same reference body (§16.2) whose `lift.retval` delivers slice j of the payload.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant), DLT-16.2
  <1>4 [req] Every W_j executes an identical ordered computation and validation of every projection, with identical row charges and fault conditions; only its last lift.retval operand differs.
  <1>5 [req] Thus all variants compute the same fault code, even when budget expires in delivery, and all copy-outs are zero on any common failure.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant)
  <1>6 [req] For a single slice, retain its existing rows and return directly without an extra projection move.
DLT-8.6-P2
  <1>1 [req] **k = 0** (no payload outputs): there is one synthetic variant **W_empty**, with T = 1.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant)
  <1>2 [req] It executes the same prologue, region body and unwind check as other variants; on success its terminal rows are `p0 = lift.const.i1 0` and `lift.retval p0` (§16.2), charged normally.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant), DLT-16.2
  <1>3 [req] The caller allocates one clean hidden target bit, invokes `oracle_call @W_empty tk (ins..) hidden fault (mem..) (args..)` exactly once using the caller's required four-wire fault register, then frees the hidden target.   deps: DLT-8.6-P2.S1 (W_empty), DLT-8.2-P7.S3 (fault register)
  <1>4 [req] The hidden bit remains zero on success and fault; it is workspace, not a payload output.
  <1>5 [req] Under invocation controls, predicate the call on all of them; allocation and free remain unconditional.
  <1>6 [req] Do not issue a second call to clean the hidden target: that would XOR away the delivered fault code.
DLT-8.6-P3
  <1>1 [req] **k = 1** (every output fits 128 bits in one register): the invocation is `oracle_call @W_0 tk (ins..) tgt fault (mem..) (args..)`.   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register)
DLT-8.6-P4
  <1>1 [req] **k > 1** (the `wide` event, §18.2): the caller's tier issues, for j = k − 1, …, 1, with slice j at bits [lo_j, lo_j + w_j) of output register o_j:   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register), DLT-18.2
  <1>2 [req] (code block, 8 lines) t_j = qreg.new any w_j ; f_j = qreg.new any 4
DLT-8.6-P5
  <1>1 [unc] followed by `s_0 = qreg.slice o_0 lo_0 w_0` and `oracle_call @W_0 tk (ins..) s_0 fault (mem..) (args..)`.
  <1>2 [req] `@xor<w>` is the permutation action `(mut s:wire[w]) (in t:wire[w]) () ()` with body `qxor t s`; each slice view is the operand of exactly one region call (ISA §3.3).   deps: DLT-2-P3.S2 (wire), ISA-3.3
DLT-8.6-P6
  <1>1 [req] Each copy-out pair computes slice j into fresh wires, XORs it into the target and uncomputes it by the identical self-adjoint call, whose inputs no call in between modifies, so `t_j` and `f_j` are clean when freed (ISA §5.2 involution; the ISA §3.3 cleanliness check of `qreg.free`); slice 0 and the fault code are delivered by the last call.   deps: DLT-2-P3.S2 (wire), ISA-5.2, ISA-3.3
  <1>2 [req] The effect is exactly NS's F_B with a wide payload: slice_j ⊕= payload_j(F_B(x)) for every j and fault ⊕= code(F_B(x)).
  <1>3 [req] Cost: 2k − 1 oracle calls (efficiency item G-15, §25.3).   deps: DLT-1.3-P1.S3 (efficiency item), DLT-25.3
  <1>4 [req] Under a `ctrl` every region call is `ctl`-prefixed (§18.2).   deps: DLT-18.2
DLT-8.6-P7
  <1>1 [req] The descriptor MUST retain independent IN, ARG, MEM_IN, OUT and INOUT bindings, packed field order, preserved inputs, common-delivery validation and exactly one synthetic invocation for zero payload outputs.   declared: DLT-8.1, DLT-8.2, DLT-8.6, DLT-16.2-P17, ISA-4.7, ISA-5.2, ISA-7.2
````

### §8.7 In-place updates   [DLT-8.7]

````text
DLT-8.7-P1
  <1>1 [req] `inplace(g, ginv, budget, desc)` binds the in-place register x as `INOUT` (exactly one parameter of each candidate pair is `INOUT`, of type `iN` with N = n(x); the result type is `iN`). g and ginv are oracles in the sense of §8.2 with a **payload equal to the new value of x**: their reference objects (§16.2) bind x as an `in` bundle and have an n(x)-bit target.   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register), DLT-16-P1.S1 (reference object), DLT-8.2, DLT-16.2
  <1>2 [req] The descriptor's `tgt` MUST be null and its `fault` is ignored (`T-IFACE` otherwise): an in-place update has no fault outcome (NS §4.2), and the `qinplace` expansion allocates its own clean scratch (ISA §4.5).   deps: ISA-4.5
DLT-8.7-P2
  <1>1 [req] **No other bindings**: an exhaustive/library-verified pair lowers to ISA `qinplace @g @ginv tk x` (ISA §4.5) with @g and @ginv the pair's reference oracles.   deps: ISA-4.5   declared: DLT-8.7-P2, DLT-8.7-P5, DLT-8.7-P6, ISA-4.5, ISA-12.1
  <1>2 [req] A sampled pair uses the CC expansion below with empty preserved-input, memory and argument lists.   deps: ~DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC)   declared: DLT-8.7-P5, DLT-8.7-P6, ISA-4.7
DLT-8.7-P3
  <1>1 [req] **Classical `ARG`s with finite value sets**: an exhaustive/library-verified tuple uses one `qinplace` with the pair specialised to those constants (arguments become `lift.const` in the reference bodies), dispatched by §14.2.   deps: ~DLT-2-P10.S1 (value set), ~DLT-14.2   declared: DLT-8.7-P3, DLT-8.7-P6, ISA-4.5, ISA-12.1

DLT-8.7-P4
  <1>1 [req] **Library bijections**: when the pair is a `bennett-arith` library bijection (add or subtract a value, xor, rotate, negate, byte swap, modular addition, modular multiplication by a unit, each with its stated conditions and its g∘ginv = id certificate, NS §3.1), the call lowers to the library's permutation action with `IN`, `MEM_IN` and `ARG` bindings as its `in`, `mem` and `args` operands, which ISA 0.8 expresses directly (ISA §4.7 `action_call`).   deps: ISA-4.7
  <1>2 [req] This is also the TDL-5(b) mechanism (§10).   deps: DLT-10-P25.S1 (TDL-5), DLT-10
DLT-8.7-P5
  <1>1 [req] **User pairs with `IN`, `MEM_IN` or arbitrary `ARG`s**: allocate clean n(x)-wire t and 4-wire f at the CC boundary.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC)
  <1>2 [req] Issue oracle_call @g tk (x, ins..) t f (mem..) (args..), exchange x and t by a swap action, then oracle_call @ginv tk (x, ins..) t f (mem..) (args..), and qreg.free t and f.
  <1>3 [req] Preserved parameter bindings are identical in both calls.
  <1>4 [req] Under control, predicate every region call including the swap; allocation/free remain unconditional.
  <1>5 [req] This is a CC-level expansion like §8.6, not an assertion that a static action passes ISA §6's coarse provenance windows.   deps: DLT-8.6, ISA-6
  <1>6 [req] Universal inverse and fault-free budget obligations below guarantee clean scratch on every basis state, hence on superpositions.
  <1>7 [req] Parameterised qinplace is efficiency only (§25.3); BLK-3 is retired.   deps: DLT-25.3
DLT-8.7-P6
  <1>1 [req] **Verification.** For every compiled pair and every argument tuple, when N ≤ the configured width (driver option `-bennett-inplace-exhaustive-bits`, default 24, §24), the plugin MUST run the reference interpreter on both reference bodies with an unbounded budget and check that for every x ∈ [0, 2^N), F^g(x) = (y, 0) and F^ginv(y) = (x, 0); it records the **minimal budget** B_min, the componentwise maximum over all those runs of (rows, heap bytes, stack cells, depth).   deps: DLT-24
  <1>2 [req] Above that width it MUST record a `sampled` evidence claim (ISA §12.1) of the same check and B_sample over the sample as an observed lower bound only, and the dynamic net applies: a wrong inverse leaves the scratch register of the `qinplace` expansion non-clean, which `T-CLEAN` catches (NS §3.1).   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register), ISA-12.1
  <1>3 [req] F_B is monotone in the budget (a run that completes within B completes identically within every B′ ≥ B), so the pair is valid for exactly B ≥ B_min only when the check is exhaustive over the full input/parameter domain.
  <1>4 [req] Sampling cannot establish B_min or universal invertibility.
  <1>5 [req] In all sampled cases validity assumes mutually inverse total functions and a sound bound B_bound covering every input and parameter value.
  <1>6 [req] A library or producer-supplied bound is permitted with an explicit correctness obligation recorded in the certificate; no mechanised proof format is required.
  <1>7 [req] B_sample never substitutes for B_bound, and T-CLEAN is not a universal budget guarantee.
  <1>8 [req] Use B_bound in the following budget checks for sampled pairs.
  <1>9 [req] A pair that fails the check, or whose budget is static and below B_min in some component, is `BD-E-INPLACE-NOT-INVERSE` (NS §3.1: "an in-place update with no inverse fails loud at compile time"; "a fallible or budget-limited computation cannot be in-place"); a run-time budget (§9.5) below B_min traps at the marker (`T-BUDGET`).   deps: DLT-22.1-P18.S1 (BD-E-INPLACE-NOT-INVERSE), DLT-9.5
  <1>10 [non] *(non-normative)* On a finite set, ginv∘g = id makes g injective, hence a bijection, so g∘ginv = id and ginv is fault-free on every input, as ISA `qinplace` requires.
  <1>11 [req] 0.1's `BD-E-INPLACE-UNVERIFIED` is deleted.
DLT-8.7-P7
  <1>1 [req] Parametrised in-place calls MUST preserve the existing CC expansion for every admitted pair.   deps: ~DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC)   declared: DLT-8.7-P5, DLT-8.7-P6, ISA-3.3-P9, ISA-4.7
DLT-8.7-P8
  <1>1 [req] Pairs admitted with sampled evidence and the recorded universal inverse and sound-bound obligations MUST retain the CC expansion, and MUST NOT be labelled a native qinplace inverse-pair proof on the strength of sampling or T-CLEAN.   deps: ~DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC)   declared: DLT-8.7-P5, DLT-8.7-P6, ISA-3.3-P9, ISA-4.7, ISA-4.5-P5, ISA-12.1-P1, ISA-12.1-P2
````

````text
  <1>3 [ex] (code block, 38 lines) define internal i8 @inc8(i8 %x) {
  <1>4 [ex] (code block, 64 lines) define internal i8 @inc8(i8 %x) {
  <1>5 [ex] (code block, 3 lines) BD-B-ISA1 @run call @__bennett_oracle(@inc8): budget field steps = 5 + a 64-bit …   deps: DLT-25.1-P3.S1 (BLK-2)
DLT-9.5-P6
  <1>1 [non] *(non-normative)* In `budget-device-computed` the oracle's budget depends on measurement outcomes: NS §4.2 "run-time budgets come from the host or from measurement results".
  <1>2 [req] `%acc2` is a loop phi over 64 measured bits, so its value set is ⊤ (it has 2^64 possible values, beyond K = 4096 atoms); it is neither static nor a bitwise copy of a launch argument, and no launch-time set of tokens covers it.   deps: DLT-2-P10.S1 (value set)
  <1>3 [req] Each wire of `%c` measured 1 is reset by an `x`, so `%c` is clean at its `qfree` (ISA §3.3).   deps: DLT-2-P3.S2 (wire), ISA-3.3
````

### §10 Taint-driven lifting under control (tdl 0.2.4)   [DLT-10]

````text
DLT-10-P1
  <1>1 [unc] NS §0: "a way to condition a region on a qubit.
  <1>2 [req] Everything else is inferred"; NS §3.1 taint row: a context-sensitive interprocedural analysis "over data dependence, control dependence and memory effects, from marker results and region entries … with polyvariant specialisation".
  <1>3 [req] This section replaces 0.1's generation-only semantics, in which classical stores of a `ctrl` body happened on both branches of the control (audit 1.4-d, R1).
  <1>4 [req] Rule ids TDL-1 to TDL-12 are normative anchors.   deps: DLT-10-P2.S1 (TDL-1), DLT-10-P47.S1 (TDL-12)
  <1>5 [req] ISA 0.8 expresses every construct below: actions call oracles (ISA §5.3, §4.7) and CC issues controlled region calls (ISA §4.7 `ctl w <call>`).   deps: DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC), ISA-5.3, ISA-4.7
DLT-10-P2
  <1>1 [req] **TDL-1 Interface vs body.** The marker fixes the interface: `ctrl`, `adj` and `compute` give an action; `oracle` and `inplace` give an oracle.
  <1>2 [req] The body of an action region is partitioned by content (TDL-3) and is never rejected for containing classical code.   deps: DLT-10-P14.S1 (TDL-3), DLT-7.1-P7.S3 (action region)
DLT-10-P3
  <1>1 [req] **TDL-2 Coherence states.**   deps: DLT-2-P13.S1 (Coherence state)
DLT-10-P4
  <1>1 [req] **Object state.** Every instance of an abstract object X has a dynamic state K(X) ∈ {Cl, M, Co}, kept by the CC tier (a runtimes table for globals, the coherent allocator's bookkeeping for heap objects; §11, §17): Cl (the CC **shadow** holds X's bytes; X's arena cells are |0⟩), M (materialised: the arena cells hold the same bytes as a basis state; both are valid), Co (the arena is the truth and may be superposed; the shadow is invalid).   deps: DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC), DLT-10-P20.S2 (coherent allocator), DLT-11, DLT-17
  <1>2 [req] Every instance starts Cl.
  <1>3 [req] Transitions: Cl → M by **materialisation** (an uncontrolled XOR of the shadow into the arena cells, TDL-4); M → Cl by the same XOR (dematerialisation, before a CC store to X); M or Cl → Co when an event is applied (§18.2) that writes X's cells with a non-empty control set or with a Co value; Co → Cl by `__bennett_observe` of all of X's bytes (TDL-11); partial observe leaves K=Co and the observed cells in their measured basis state.   deps: DLT-10-P19.S1 (TDL-4), DLT-10-P43.S1 (TDL-11), DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC), DLT-18.2-P1.S1 (control set), DLT-18.2
  <1>4 [req] Coverage is tracked since each byte's last write; writes invalidate coverage except a permitted TDL-11 CC store to already-covered bytes.   deps: DLT-10-P43.S1 (TDL-11), DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC)
  <1>5 [req] That store writes a known classical value to both arena and shadow, so the bytes remain covered with that store as their covering write.
  <1>6 [req] Release never changes Co to Cl by fiat: first restore the cells to the basis value equal to the shadow with the invocation's own events, then dematerialise to Cl and release.
  <1>7 [req] Otherwise release traps T-TAINT-HOST (code 4), inside or outside generation, before reuse.
DLT-10-P5
  <1>1 [req] **Value state.** During a generation (§18.4) every executed SSA value instance is Cl or Co: Co iff it is a deferred measurement result (§7.5a), a load of a byte whose **view** (below) is Co, the result of an instruction with a Co operand, or a `phi` at the join of a Co branch.   deps: DLT-7.5-P2.S1 (deferred measurement), DLT-18.4, DLT-7.5-P2
DLT-10-P6
  <1>1 [req] **View.** A generation sees outliving memory through a **view**: a byte of object X has view Co if K(X) = Co, or if the generation's recorder (or a recorder of an enclosing generation of the same invocation) holds an event that writes it with a non-empty control set or with a Co value; otherwise its view is Cl.   deps: DLT-18.2-P1.S1 (control set)

  <1>3 [req] The enclosing invocation control is added only at event composition, not to this inherited view.
  <1>4 [req] This applies to nested ctrl, adj and compute; sibling arm recorders stay isolated until join.

  <1>6 [req] Its classical events update use's Cl view; its predicated or Co-valued writes give use a Co view.

DLT-10-P8

DLT-10-P16

DLT-10-P17

  <1>1 [req] **TDL-4 Coherent arena.**

  <1>1 [req] Exact; no history.

  <1>9 [req] Classical twins charge their executed instructions.
  <1>10 [req] Compilation never runs G to completion to discover an event list: G is a bounded CC routine executed at invocation.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC)
````

````text
DLT-11.3-P1
  <1>1 [req] In an L variant, an effect marker call becomes a call of the runtimes function `__bennett_dev_<model>_<op>` with the same operands.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant), DLT-3.5-P1.S1 (marker call)

DLT-11.3-P2
  <1>1 [req] `entropy` | base = `lift.addr @e0`, size = 2^A bytes, pos = 0 | `read(p, len)`: if len > size − pos, `__bennett_nz_fault(10)` (`FAULT_ENTROPY_EXHAUSTED`); else copy [base + pos, base + pos + len) to p and pos += len
DLT-11.3-P3
  <1>1 [req] `block` | base = `lift.addr @k0`, nsect = 2^A′; an empty overlay | `read(s, p)`: the overlay's 512 bytes for sector s if present, else sector s of the region if s < nsect, else 512 zero bytes (ISA §7.3: absent sectors read as zero); `write(s, p)`: copy 512 bytes into the overlay entry for s (a heap allocation by `malloc`, lifted to `lift.alloc`)   deps: ISA-7.3
DLT-11.3-P4

DLT-11.3-P5

DLT-11.3-P6
````

````text
DLT-11.5-P1
  <1>1 [req] ISA 0.8 does not specify which code a CC trap reports.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC)

  <1>4 [req] Typed R faults therefore have dependency blocker BLK-5 = ISA-7 (§25.1).   deps: DLT-25.1-P4.S1 (BLK-5), DLT-25.2-P3.S1 (ISA-7), DLT-25.1
DLT-11.5-P2

  <1>2 [req] Every such variant has the §17.6 budget check, regardless of supplied run-time limits.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant), DLT-17.6
  <1>3 [req] A reversible call treated as a direct call under §7.4 is not an R entry and does not by itself block.   deps: DLT-7.4
  <1>4 [req] Other rejection/blocker precedence remains §1.6.   deps: DLT-1.6
  <1>5 [req] The R blocker trap is generic ISA trap with no hostcall, reached only on executions that would report a typed fault (budget exhaustion, F(C), nz_fault(C)); all other executions are unaffected.   deps: DLT-1.6-P4.S2 (blocker trap)
  <1>6 [req] This fallback does not implement typed reporting.
DLT-11.5-P3
  <1>1 [req] Required operation: R fault C terminates with fault record code C, performs no subsequent source effect and preserves reversible prefix history.
````

### §12.1 Scope, order and naming   [DLT-12.1]

````text
DLT-12.1-P1
  <1>1 [req] The normaliser rewrites every device variant (§4.3) and the initialisers of every global a device variant references; H variants are untouched.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant), DLT-4.3
  <1>2 [req] It applies the rules of §12.2 in table order, each to the whole module before the next, with one exception: N33 is applied immediately before N32 so any floating-point instructions introduced by its expansions are processed by N32; own-format carrier calls and bit-exact reconstruction remain as specified in §13.4.   deps: DLT-12.2-P35.S1 (N33), DLT-12.2-P34.S1 (N32), DLT-12.2, DLT-13.4
  <1>3 [req] After N27 and N32, re-apply N22 to every instruction they created with an integer side wider than 128 bits.   deps: DLT-12.2-P29.S1 (N27), DLT-12.2-P34.S1 (N32), DLT-12.2-P24.S1 (N22)
  <1>4 [req] Only width legalisation repeats; no other rule re-runs.
  <1>5 [req] Width lowering may be fused with an expansion when the resulting canonical limb rows are identical.
  <1>6 [def] The result is the **materialised module**: the reference semantics (§18), the lifting map (§16) and the native comparison build (§17.7) are all defined on it (NS §3.2: "the native comparison binary is built from that materialised bitcode").   deps: DLT-17.7-P1.S1 (native comparison binary), DLT-18, DLT-16, DLT-17.7
DLT-12.1-P2
  <1>1 [req] **Naming.** A rule that introduces a value names it `%nz.<tag>.<r>`, where `<r>` is the name of the instruction being rewritten without its `%` (a number for an unnamed value).
  <1>2 [req] For a rewritten instruction without a result (a `void` call, a `store`, an `invoke` of a `void` function), `<r>` is `<f>.<k>`: f the enclosing function's name and k the 0-based count, in instruction order, of the result-less instructions of f that the same rule rewrites.
  <1>3 [req] A value introduced once per function is `%nz.<tag>.<f>`.
  <1>4 [req] A constant global a rule needs is `@nz.<tag>.<f>.<r>`.
  <1>5 [req] A declaration a rule needs is appended at the end of the module, and a global after the module's globals, in order of first use.
  <1>6 [req] Each rule states its tags.
````

### §12.3 Fault replacement F(C)   [DLT-12.3]

````text
DLT-12.3-P1
  <1>1 [req] F(C): the instruction is replaced by `call void @__bennett_nz_fault(i64 C)` followed by `unreachable`; the instructions after it in its block are deleted, and the block is removed from the incoming lists of the phi nodes of its former successors.
  <1>2 [req] `__bennett_nz_fault` is a primitive (§3.1): `bennett-runtimes` defines it for the native comparison build (record C and end the device entry with fault C); the map gives it the row `fault C` (§16.4); CC and R lower it by §11.5.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC), DLT-3.1, DLT-16.4, DLT-11.5
````

### §12.5 Scalable vectors   [DLT-12.5]

````text
DLT-12.5-P1
  <1>1 [req] A scalable vector type `<vscale x L x T>` has L·V lanes, where V is the constant `vscale` of the link: the function attribute `vscale_range(V, V)` when every device function that uses scalable vectors carries it with equal bounds, else the driver option `--bennett-vscale=<V>` (default: the minimum of the `vscale_range` bounds, §24).   deps: DLT-24
  <1>2 [req] The native comparison build is compiled for the same V (`-msve-vector-bits=128·V` or `-mrvv-vector-bits`).
  <1>3 [req] N10 replaces `llvm.vscale` by V and N21 scalarises the L·V lanes.   deps: DLT-12.2-P12.S1 (N10), DLT-12.2-P23.S1 (N21)
  <1>4 [non] *(non-normative)* x86-64 has no scalable vectors; the rule exists so that AArch64 SVE and RISC-V V code is liftable.
````

### §12.6 Vector scalarisation (N21)   [DLT-12.6]

````text
DLT-12.6-P1
  <1>1 [req] For a value `%v` of type `<L x T>`, lane k is the scalar `%nz.l<k>.v` (k = 0 … L − 1).
  <1>2 [req] Rules, in lane order k = 0, 1, …:
DLT-12.6-P2
  <1>1 [req] elementwise instructions (binary, bitwise, `icmp`, `fcmp`, casts, `select` with a vector or scalar condition, unary `fneg`, `freeze`, calls of elementwise intrinsics): one scalar instruction per lane, `%nz.l<k>.r = <op> T %nz.l<k>.a, %nz.l<k>.b`;
DLT-12.6-P3

  <1>4 [req] Zero-extend source carriers to total width, shift by cumulative widths and OR in source-lane order; extract by logical right shift and truncation in destination-lane order.
  <1>5 [req] Omit identity casts and zero shifts; N22 legalises total widths above 128.   deps: DLT-12.2-P24.S1 (N22)
  <1>6 [req] Drop no source memory access.

  <1>3 [req] Otherwise byte-sized lanes use `getelementptr i8, ptr p, i64 (k·bitwidth(T)/8)`; sub-byte lanes use packed-byte extraction/insertion.
  <1>4 [req] Replacement accesses stay within the original vector storage range.
````

````text
  <1>3 [non] *(non-normative)* `fneg`, `fabs` and `copysign` stay bit-exact, so a NaN's sign bit set by `fneg` survives, as LangRef requires; an implementation of `half` and `bfloat` + − × ÷ √ in binary32 followed by one rounding is correctly rounded, since 24 ≥ 2p + 2 for p = 11 and p = 8 (Figueroa's double-rounding bound), but the contract is correct rounding, so `fma` needs its own implementation.
````

````text
DLT-16.3-P7
  <1>1 [req] for the q-th indirect call of block i (q ≥ 1): the leaf of candidate k (sorted order), the default, the continuation | `^b<i>.q<q>c<k>`, `^b<i>.q<q>d`, `^b<i>.q<q>r`
DLT-16.3-P8
  <1>1 [req] the edge block from block i to block s | `^b<i>.e<s>`   deps: DLT-16.4-P38.S3 (edge block)
DLT-16.3-P9
  <1>1 [req] the n-th global of the layout (1-based, in link order) | data symbol and global `G<n>`
DLT-16.3-P10
  <1>1 [req] The `regs` line lists every location of the function that is neither a parameter nor the result, in order of first appearance as a destination in the text, as `name:reg[W]`, separated by `, `; it is omitted when empty.
  <1>2 [req] W: a value's width (`i1` → 1, `ptr addrspace(a)` → P(a)); a constant's width; a temporary's width (1 for a compare, else its operation's width).
DLT-16.3-P11
  <1>1 [req] **Layout.** The reference object's `layout` is the device link layout (§19.5) restricted to the non-arena globals that the L closure names in `lift.addr` and, transitively, non-arena globals their initialisers point to (in link order, numbered G1, G2, …), with the link's `ptr_width`, `null_size`, `heap_base`, `heap_limit_max`, `H`, `A_tab` and `S_cells`, and `interface_regions` = { "ref": the shape's regions }.   deps: DLT-16-P1.S1 (reference object), DLT-19.5

  <1>5 [req] H is the smallest value with every range inside [0, 2^H); A_tab is the smallest value with 2^A_tab ≥ P + `heap_limit_max`, P the link's number of globals plus the largest number of interface regions of any oracle, so that allocation-table overflow never precedes heap exhaustion (both fault with code 2, ISA §4.2, and a reference object with fewer pre-entries than the device object faults at the same allocation); S_cells is the smallest value with 2^S_cells ≥ the frozen `stack` capacity of §9.2.   deps: DLT-16-P1.S1 (reference object), ISA-4.2, DLT-9.2
  <1>6 [req] These link capacities are frozen before provisional identity construction and include unmatched raw entries and static non-sentinel record fields; identity overlays never recompute them.
````

### §16.4 Rows   [DLT-16.4]

````text
DLT-16.4-P1
  <1>1 [req] Pointer constants, flattened pointer fields, parameters, results and pointer memory values use P(a), including their DataLayout storage size.
  <1>2 [req] Materialise null at P(a).
  <1>3 [req] Before an ISA memory address operand, bridge the source pointer representation to pw with the target's address conversion (zero-extension/truncation for the integral flat-address spaces); this bridge never changes the stored pointer width or the source ptrtoint/inttoptr semantics.
  <1>4 [req] Apply the same rules to constant expressions and the native comparison build.
  <1>5 [req] Representations above 128 bits use §12.7 limbs; mixed-width layouts are not rejected.   deps: DLT-12.7
DLT-16.4-P2
  <1>1 [req] Every row accessing program memory first performs TDL-4's logical validation if the address can be in coh, before the physical ISA boundscheck.   deps: DLT-10-P19.S1 (TDL-4)
  <1>2 [req] Loads and stores, including slice/event producers, use the same helper and fault gating.
  <1>3 [req] Proved containment in a static arena global (as in arena-o1's one-byte @cnt load) discharges this check without extra rows; a physical coh entry alone is never such a proof.
  <1>4 [req] For an address that can lie in shadow-stack backing storage, also perform §17.3's logical-frame check before every program load, store or memory-function access, including non-coh addresses.   deps: DLT-17.3
  <1>5 [req] The materialised __bennett_rt_ss_check(p,n,table) helper's comparisons, calls and fault rows count normally.
  <1>6 [req] Gate mutations and dependent events on its success.
  <1>7 [req] Physical boundscheck/load/store rows remain required; they do not substitute for the logical check.
  <1>8 [req] Explicit runtime-internal bookkeeping uses the internal path of §17.3, not the program-access helper.   deps: DLT-17.3
DLT-16.4-P3
  <1>1 [req] Rows of an instruction are emitted in instruction order within its block.
  <1>2 [req] Before the rows of an instruction, each of its **constant operands** that is a value operand (in operand order; not an immediate flag; for `getelementptr`, not a constant index) is materialised: an integer constant by `c<j> = lift.const.iW <unsigned decimal>`; `null` by `lift.const.i<P(a)> 0`; a non-arena global `@G` by `c<j> = lift.addr @G<n>`; an arena global by `c<j> = lift.addr @coh`, and if its arena offset δ is nonzero, `c<j+1> = lift.const.i<pw> δ`, `t<j> = lift.add c<j> c<j+1>` (the operand reads this temporary); in an lproc the base is its hidden arena-base parameter rather than lift.addr @coh.
  <1>3 [req] The wrapper materialises @coh once before the region call, appends this pw-bit argument after source parameters, and every transitive lproc call threads it unchanged.
  <1>4 [req] Only functions in the arena-reading closure receive it; materialising the base in a lproc uses lift.mov of that parameter.
  <1>5 [req] Materialise a function `@F` by `c<j> = lift.const.i<pw> <A(F)>`; a constant expression by the rows of its instructions, innermost first, into temporaries.
  <1>6 [req] The operand then reads `c<j>`.
  <1>7 [req] Aggregate constants materialise one scalar carrier constant per flattened field in field order before packing.
  <1>8 [req] A non-constant operand reads the location of its value (`a<i>` for a parameter).
  <1>9 [req] `A`, `B`, `C` below are the operands so read; `v` is the instruction's location.
DLT-16.4-P4
  <1>1 [req] `add sub mul and or xor shl lshr ashr` | `v = lift.<op> A B`
DLT-16.4-P5
  <1>1 [req] `udiv sdiv urem srem` | `v = lift.<op> A B` (division faults, ISA §4.2)   deps: ISA-4.2
DLT-16.4-P6
  <1>1 [req] `icmp eq/ne/ult/ule/slt/sle a, b` (integers or pointers) | `v = lift.icmp.<pred> A B`
DLT-16.4-P7
  <1>1 [req] `icmp ugt/uge/sgt/sge a, b` | `v = lift.icmp.{ult,ule,slt,sle} B A` (operands swapped)
DLT-16.4-P8
  <1>1 [req] `select c, a, b` | `v = lift.select C A B`
DLT-16.4-P9
  <1>1 [req] `zext/sext/trunc a to iM` | `v = lift.<op>.iM A`
DLT-16.4-P10
  <1>1 [req] `ptrtoint` to iM, `inttoptr` from iM | Let P=P(a) for the pointer operand/result.
  <1>2 [req] M = P: `v = lift.mov A`; ptrtoint M < P or inttoptr M > P: `lift.trunc` to the destination width; otherwise `lift.zext` to the destination width (LangRef zero-extends)
DLT-16.4-P11
  <1>1 [req] `bitcast` of equal-width integer/FP carriers or pointers | `v = lift.mov A`; FP constants materialise their carrier bit pattern
DLT-16.4-P12
  <1>1 [req] `addrspacecast` | materialise the incoming target's specified conversion between address-space representations, including any non-width conversion; `lift.mov` only for bit-preserving equal-width conversions.
  <1>2 [req] For integral zero-extend/truncate conversions emit `lift.zext`/`lift.trunc` to P(destination)
DLT-16.4-P13
  <1>1 [req] `getelementptr T, ptr p, idx…` | Let P=P(a), I=I(a) for p's address space.
  <1>2 [req] Arithmetic on the low I bits is modulo 2^I; only representation bits above I are preserved, also for constant expressions.
  <1>3 [req] Canonical rows: acc is the pointer operand (when I<P, first `t = lift.trunc.i<I> P_operand` and acc is t).
  <1>4 [req] For each non-constant sequential index in index order: sign-extend/truncate to I (omit the cast when already I wide); if its element allocation size s≠1 emit `c = lift.const.i<I> (s mod 2^I)` then `t = lift.mul index c`, else use the index directly; emit `acc′ = lift.add acc t`.
  <1>5 [req] Constant sequential indices, interpreted signed at their source width then scaled by s, and constant structure field offsets accumulate into Δ mod 2^I, with no per-index rows.
  <1>6 [req] After the dynamic sequence, if Δ≠0 emit `c = lift.const.i<I> Δ` then `acc′ = lift.add acc c`.
  <1>7 [req] For I=P the last acc′ row writes v; with no dynamic index and Δ=0 the only row is `v = lift.mov P_operand`.
  <1>8 [req] For I<P always emit recombination, even when acc equals trunc(P_operand), in this order: `lo = lift.zext.i<P> acc`; `c = lift.const.i<P> <ones above I>`; `hi = lift.and P_operand c`; `v = lift.or hi lo`.
  <1>9 [req] Every emitted row is charged normally
DLT-16.4-P14
  <1>1 [req] `load T, ptr p` (T = iN with N a multiple of 8, or `ptr`; N ≤ 128 after §12; FP uses its carrier) | `lift.boundscheck P <N/8>`; `v = lift.load.iN P`   deps: DLT-12
DLT-16.4-P15
  <1>1 [req] `store v, ptr p` | `lift.boundscheck P <N/8>`; `lift.store.iN P V`
DLT-16.4-P16
  <1>1 [req] `insertvalue`, `extractvalue` | `lift.mov` of the depth-first flattened field locations (one per scalar field); unchanged fields remain their input locations
DLT-16.4-P17
  <1>1 [req] FP `load`, `store`, `select`, `phi` | the corresponding integer-carrier row, bit-exact
DLT-16.4-P18
  <1>1 [req] `fneg`, `llvm.fabs`, `llvm.copysign` | for IEEE/x87 formats, xor sign mask / and complement sign mask / clear magnitude sign then or source sign, at carrier width (sign bit 15, 31, 63, 79 or 127).
  <1>2 [req] For ppc_fp128, fneg flips both component signs; fabs conditionally flips both using the high double's sign; copysign conditionally flips both according to differing high signs, preserving APFloat PPCDoubleDouble semantics
DLT-16.4-P19
  <1>1 [req] aggregate `ret` of packed width ≤128 | zext each field to packed width (identity if equal), shift by cumulative prior field widths (omit zero shift), or in field order; `lift.ret` packed value
DLT-16.4-P20
  <1>1 [req] aggregate call result | `lift.call` into a packed-width temporary, then for each field lshr by cumulative offset (omit zero shift), trunc to field width (identity if equal)
DLT-16.4-P21
  <1>1 [req] `phi` | none at its position (edge moves)
DLT-16.4-P22
````

### §17.1 Memory model   [DLT-17.1]

````text
DLT-17.1-P1
  <1>1 [req] There is one classical memory, shared by H, CC, R and the entry state of every L invocation (§8.5; NS §3.2):   deps: DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC), DLT-8.5
DLT-17.1-P2
  <1>1 [def] **Live allocations**: a shadow-stack frame from its push to its pop (§17.3); a global, always; a heap allocation of the runtimes allocator from its allocation to its `free` (`free` of a null pointer does nothing).   deps: DLT-17.3
  <1>2 [req] The null region is never allocated.
DLT-17.1-P3
  <1>1 [req] **Zero fill**: shadow-stack frames and heap allocations are zero-filled in both builds; globals hold their initialisers.
  <1>2 [req] Region inputs are not zero-filled: they are the bytes the host supplies (NS §3.2).
DLT-17.1-P4
  <1>1 [req] **Bounds**: a load, store or memory-function range is valid iff all its bytes lie in one live allocation (an address model: the object a pointer was derived from is irrelevant; NS §3.2 "faulting memory access is defined").
DLT-17.1-P5
  <1>1 [req] **Addresses**: the comparison link (§19.5) places globals and functions; the runtimes allocator's fixed base places the heap; the shadow stack is heap memory, so native stack addresses never reach device results.   deps: DLT-4.4-P1.S1 (comparison link), DLT-19.5
  <1>2 [req] The residue is host-stack addresses passed in by host code: executions in which they influence a result are *layout-dependent* (NS §3.2; §24 D12), validated against the reference interpreter.   deps: DLT-24-P2.S1 (D12), DLT-24
DLT-17.1-P6
  <1>1 [req] **Single thread**: atomics and volatile are sequentialised (N9; NS §3.2; §24 D24).   deps: DLT-12.2-P11.S1 (N9), DLT-24-P8.S1 (D24), DLT-24
````

### §17.3 Shadow stack (N24)   [DLT-17.3]

````text
DLT-17.3-P1
  <1>1 [req] NS §3.2: "Region allocas are rewritten by the normaliser onto a shim-managed shadow stack in both builds where possible"; in device variants it is always possible.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant)
  <1>2 [req] The runtimes provide, with these contracts:
DLT-17.3-P2
  <1>1 [req] `void __bennett_rt_ss_init(i64 size)` | is idempotent: if stack state is already set (by entry replay in an oracle), allocates nothing and keeps base, size and stack pointer; otherwise allocates one heap block of `size` bytes (`sstack`, §9.2), by `__bennett_nz_alloc`; called by the oracle wrapper prologue (§16.2), the R entry stub and the CC entry stub when their closure uses the shadow stack   deps: DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC), DLT-9.2, DLT-16.2
DLT-17.3-P3
  <1>1 [req] `ptr __bennett_rt_ss_push(i64 size, i64 align)` | pushes a frame of `size` bytes aligned to `align` and returns its base; the frame is zero-filled; overflow of the block is `__bennett_nz_fault(2)` (`FAULT_BUDGET_HEAP`)
DLT-17.3-P4
  <1>1 [req] `void __bennett_rt_ss_pop(ptr fp)` | pops the frame fp and every frame pushed after it
DLT-17.3-P5
  <1>1 [req] `ptr __bennett_rt_ss_alloca(i64 n, i64 align)` | a zero-filled dynamic allocation in the current frame, released by its pop
DLT-17.3-P6
  <1>1 [req] `ptr __bennett_rt_ss_save()`, `void __bennett_rt_ss_restore(ptr)` | `llvm.stacksave`/`llvm.stackrestore`
DLT-17.3-P7
  <1>1 [req] Shadow-stack backing storage is physical storage, not a program allocation.
  <1>2 [req] Maintain logical frame base, extent and liveness, including dynamic allocations, extensions and saved restore points.
  <1>3 [req] A program access requires its entire nonwrapping byte range inside one live logical frame/allocation under §17.1; otherwise fault 7 before any access or mutation.   deps: DLT-17.1
  <1>4 [req] Containment in the backing ISA allocation is insufficient.
  <1>5 [req] Push registers a live frame; pop invalidates it and every younger frame; restore invalidates released ranges, truncating a surviving dynamic extent at the saved limit.   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register)
  <1>6 [req] Separate dynamic allocations in a frame keep their individual extents; an access may not span distinct live frames/allocations or unused capacity.
  <1>7 [req] The address model permits a reused address once a new live logical allocation contains the complete range.
DLT-17.3-P8
  <1>1 [req] The default validation is the ordinary materialised runtime helper __bennett_rt_ss_check(p,n,table): reject wrapping ranges, visit logical entries in creation order, OR the live-and-contained predicates, and fault 7 if false.
  <1>2 [req] Its rows and metadata updates are charged in §16's reference object, and both builds implement the same checks and stack layout.   deps: DLT-16-P1.S1 (reference object), DLT-16
  <1>3 [req] Proven containment may eliminate the helper.
  <1>4 [req] Runtime bookkeeping, zero-fill and entry replay use an explicit internal path restricted to backing storage and metadata, never exposed to source program accesses; it is not a blanket exemption for ordinary calls into runtime-named functions.
  <1>5 [req] Replay the logical metadata as well as backing bytes under §8.5.   deps: DLT-8.5
DLT-17.3-P9
  <1>1 [req] N24 rewrites each function with allocas: `%nz.fp.<f> = call ptr @__bennett_rt_ss_push(i64 S, i64 A)` at entry, where the static allocas of the entry block are laid out in instruction order, each at the next offset aligned to its alignment, S is the total rounded up to A, the largest alignment.   deps: DLT-12.2-P26.S1 (N24)
  <1>2 [req] The pushed frame base is aligned to A; its end (the next frame start before any additional alignment) is base + S.
  <1>3 [req] Each static alloca becomes `getelementptr i8, ptr %nz.fp.<f>, i64 <offset>` with the alloca's name; every other alloca becomes `__bennett_rt_ss_alloca`; `call void @__bennett_rt_ss_pop(ptr %nz.fp.<f>)` precedes every `ret` (including the early returns of §14.4).   deps: DLT-14.4
  <1>4 [req] `llvm.frameaddress(0)`, `llvm.sponentry`, `llvm.addressofreturnaddress`, `llvm.swift.async.context.addr` and `llvm.eh.dwarf.cfa` give `%nz.fp.<f>`; `llvm.frameaddress(n > 0)` and `llvm.returnaddress` give null (LangRef: "zero if it cannot be identified"); `llvm.stackaddress` gives the current shadow-stack pointer; `llvm.localescape` records the escaped allocas' offsets in a per-function table that `llvm.localrecover` reads with the parent's frame address; `llvm.structured.alloca` is an alloca.
````

### §17.7 The native comparison build   [DLT-17.7]

````text
DLT-17.7-P1
  <1>1 [req] Differential testing (NS §5.1) compares the artefact with the **native comparison binary**: the materialised device variants, code-generated by the same LLVM major and linked with `bennett-runtimes` and `bennett-arith` (never host libc or libm) under the comparison link of §19.5.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant), DLT-4.4-P1.S1 (comparison link), DLT-19.5
  <1>2 [req] It is never an `-O0` build: optimisation legally changes marker operands (spike F4), and the materialised optimised module is the one program both builds implement.
  <1>3 [req] The driver MUST make division by zero and INT_MIN/−1 trap in the native build: on targets whose divide instruction does not trap it inserts, after materialisation and outside the materialised module, a check that calls `__bennett_nz_fault` with code 5 or 6.   deps: DLT-12.1-P1.S6 (materialised module)
  <1>4 [req] Results compare by the outcome table of §18.7.   deps: DLT-18.7
````

````text

DLT-18.1-P2

DLT-18.1-P3
  <1>1 [req] **Q**, the quantum state of the ISA formal model (ISA §14.2): a unit vector over the live wires in allocation order, including the arena's wires (TDL-4);   deps: DLT-10-P19.S1 (TDL-4), DLT-2-P3.S2 (wire), ISA-14.2
DLT-18.1-P4

DLT-18.1-P5

DLT-18.1-P6

DLT-18.1-P7

DLT-18.1-P8
````

### §18.2 Events   [DLT-18.2]

````text
DLT-18.2-P1
  <1>1 [req] A marker call or a TDL store produces **events**: ISA-level operations, each with a **control set** (a set of wires, initially empty).   deps: DLT-3.5-P1.S1 (marker call), DLT-2-P3.S2 (wire)
  <1>2 [req] The forms are:
DLT-18.2-P2
  <1>1 [req] `qalloc H n`, `qfree H`; the gates `x h s sdg t tdg cx cz swap ccx` (ISA §4.4) and `rx θ`, `ry θ`, `rz θ` on wires; `qload D M A`, `qstore M A V`, `qprep H bytes`;   deps: DLT-2-P3.S2 (wire), ISA-4.4
DLT-18.2-P3
  <1>1 [req] `oracle R B (ins..) tgt fault (mem..) (args..)` and `wide R …` (§8.6), `inplace G G′ B X`;   deps: DLT-8.6
DLT-18.2-P4
  <1>1 [req] the TDL events of §10: `slice O (args..) (ins..) (mem..) -> regs`, `xmask X+o m`, `xstore X+a m`, `perm P X+a (params..)`, `xchg X+a h`, `fault C` (TDL-12), `firstfault (f..) Φ`;   deps: DLT-10-P47.S1 (TDL-12), DLT-10
DLT-18.2-P5
  <1>1 [req] `qcopy S -> D`: allocate D clean then XOR S into it; `quncopy S D`: XOR S into D and release clean D; `qxor S T`: T XOR= S; `copy F -> G` means qalloc G then qxor F G (TDL-8);   deps: DLT-10-P36.S1 (TDL-8)
DLT-18.2-P6
  <1>1 [req] `observe X+o len`, `measure` (outside generations), `effect dev.op` (R).
DLT-18.2-P7
  <1>1 [req] When no recorder is active, an event is **applied** to Σ at once; otherwise it is appended to the innermost recorder.
  <1>2 [req] Applying an event with control set S applies it only on the basis states where every wire of S is 1 (ISA `ctl`, ISA §4.7, §5.3); `qalloc` and `qfree` are unconditional (ISA §3.5).   deps: DLT-18.2-P1.S1 (control set), DLT-2-P3.S2 (wire), ISA-4.7, ISA-5.3, ISA-3.5
  <1>3 [req] Arena writes with nonempty control set, Co address or Co value first materialise Cl objects and make Cl or M objects Co.   deps: DLT-2-P13.S3 (Arena), DLT-18.2-P1.S1 (control set)
  <1>4 [req] Otherwise apply events per form: `xmask` XORs its mask into shadow only for Cl (arena stays zero), both copies for M, arena only for Co; `xstore` does the same XOR at its selected address; `perm` applies its bijection to shadow only for Cl, both copies for M, arena only for Co.
  <1>5 [req] `xchg` with a Co register first materialises and makes X Co; with a classical basis operand it exchanges with shadow for Cl, both copies consistently for M (returning one old value), arena only for Co.   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register)
  <1>6 [req] Unconditional Cl-valued xmask/xstore/perm leave K unchanged.
  <1>7 [req] Event application does not also reapply its speculative generation-view update.
  <1>8 [req] Event-application writes invalidate observation coverage; permitted TDL-11 CC stores retain it as covering writes.   deps: DLT-10-P43.S1 (TDL-11), DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC)
  <1>9 [req] The plugin realises applied events as CC-level region calls in event order (ISA §4.7), whose temporaries are released by `qreg.free` with the dynamic cleanliness check of ISA §3.3; it MAY compile an event list into one ISA action when that action satisfies ISA §6.   deps: ISA-4.7, ISA-3.3, ISA-6
DLT-18.2-P8
  <1>1 [req] **Adjoint** of an event list (ISA §5.3 adjoint table): reverse the list and replace each event: `x h cx cz swap ccx qload qstore qprep oracle wide slice xmask xstore xchg` are self-adjoint; `s` ↔ `sdg`; `t` ↔ `tdg`; `rx θ` ↦ `rx −θ` (and `ry`, `rz`); `qalloc` ↔ `qfree` of the same wires; `inplace G G′ B X` ↦ `inplace G′ G B X`; `perm P` ↦ the library inverse of P.   deps: DLT-2-P3.S2 (wire), ISA-5.3
  <1>2 [req] Control sets are unchanged.
  <1>3 [req] Ordinary workspace qcopy and quncopy are mutual adjoints.
  <1>4 [req] A deferred-measurement qcopy is a channel record and is never adjointed to quncopy.
  <1>5 [req] In standalone adj(f), keep non-record events in reverse-list order.
  <1>6 [req] Insert each fresh retained record immediately before its earliest reversed consumer, after every reversed event preceding that consumer.
  <1>7 [req] A record without consumers stays at its reversed source position.
  <1>8 [req] Records in the same insertion gap follow original source order, with record producers before dependent records.
  <1>9 [req] Thus record placement is deterministic, including when noncommuting events change its source.
  <1>10 [req] For local sources, hoist required unconditional inverse allocations before their copies and retain the sources through their last use; this lifetime extension does not commute a copy across an arbitrary quantum operation.
  <1>11 [req] Optimisations MUST preserve this complete instrument and the §7.5(a) measurement boundary.   deps: DLT-7.5-P2
  <1>12 [req] In compute(f,use), E_f's records survive E_u and adjoint(E_f), which reuses these wires without copying or uncopying them, and measurement is at the first §7.5(a) boundary after compute returns.   deps: DLT-2-P3.S2 (wire), DLT-7.5-P2
DLT-18.2-P9
  <1>1 [req] A Co-loop adjoint is the inverse of the complete clean-workspace transition, not forward evaluation of the guard on the adjoint-entry mutable data.
  <1>2 [req] For conditions on preserved inputs, compute flags forward, apply body adjoints for i=N..1, then uncompute the flags with their exact computing slices.
  <1>3 [req] For overwritten inputs in a standalone adj, use the bounded inverse required by TDL-5(b) to reconstruct the unique forward entry on copies, compute its trajectory, apply the inverse iterations, and clean that reconstruction against the restored entry.   deps: DLT-10-P25.S1 (TDL-5)
  <1>4 [req] No assumed earlier invocation supplies this entry.
  <1>5 [req] When no unique inverse exists on the declared interface, the existing TDL-5(d) applies; changing adj into an entry-guard instrument is not an alternative inverse.   deps: DLT-10-P25.S1 (TDL-5)
  <1>6 [req] Out-of-place evaluation and compute retain the computation under TDL-5(c). compute's adjoint(E_f) reuses the actual forward flags/history and cleans them as each iteration state is restored, without a fresh trajectory.   deps: DLT-10-P25.S1 (TDL-5)
  <1>7 [req] Only genuine measurement records and actual fault outputs have their separate retained lifetimes.
DLT-18.2-P10
  <1>1 [req] qxor and firstfault are self-adjoint XORs.
  <1>2 [req] `fault C` is an xmask of C on a fresh declared fault register, also self-adjoint.   deps: DLT-10-P36.S3 (declared fault register)
  <1>3 [req] Adjoint of `copy F -> G` is qxor F G then qfree G, not another allocation.
````

````text

DLT-18.3-P2

DLT-18.3-P3
  <1>1 [req] `qborrow(cls, n)` | as `qalloc` | inside a generation compiled as an ISA action, ISA `qborrow`/`qreturn` with borrow-frame verification (ISA §5.6); otherwise as `qalloc` (a correct user of borrowed wires also works on clean wires; ISA-9, §25.3).   deps: DLT-2-P3.S2 (wire), ISA-5.6, DLT-25.3
  <1>2 [req] 0.1's `T-BORROW` is deleted
DLT-18.3-P4
  <1>1 [req] `qfree(h)` | h live (`T-DEAD`); if a recorder is active, h belongs to it (`T-FOREIGN`); when applied, Q is the product of the all-zero state on h's wires and a state of the other wires (`T-CLEAN`) | event `qfree h`   deps: DLT-2-P3.S2 (wire)
DLT-18.3-P5
  <1>1 [req] `gate(op, h, i)` | h live (`T-DEAD`); i < n(h) (`T-INDEX`); op in the table (`T-OP`) | the realisation of §3.4 on `h.i`   deps: DLT-3.4
DLT-18.3-P6
  <1>1 [req] `gate2(op, a, i, b, j)` | as above for both; `a.i` ≠ `b.j` (`T-ALIAS`) | `cx a.i b.j`, `cz a.i b.j` or `swap a.i b.j`
DLT-18.3-P7
  <1>1 [req] `gate3(op, a, i, b, j, c, k)` | as above; the three wires distinct (`T-ALIAS`) | `ccx a.i b.j c.k`   deps: DLT-2-P3.S2 (wire)
DLT-18.3-P8

DLT-18.3-P9

DLT-18.3-P10
  <1>1 [req] `qload(dst, mem, addr)` | the three handles live and distinct (`T-DEAD`, `T-ALIAS`); n(mem) = 2^n(addr) · n(dst) (`T-SIZE`) | event `qload`: for every cell c, on the basis states where addr holds c, `dst.b ⊕= mem.(c·W + b)` for b < W = n(dst) (ISA §4.6 cell order)   deps: ISA-4.6
DLT-18.3-P11

DLT-18.3-P12

DLT-18.3-P13
````

### §18.4 Generation of action regions   [DLT-18.4]

````text
DLT-18.4-P1
  <1>1 [req] `gen(R, env)` pushes a recorder, runs `R(env)`'s CC variant under §18.1 with the TDL partition of §10 (its G instructions run once on the generation's view; its slices, stores to outliving objects and marker calls produce events per §10 and §18.3, nested `ctrl`, `adj` and `compute` producing their events into this recorder), pops the recorder and returns its event list E.   deps: DLT-2-P7.S1 (CC), DLT-2-P7.S2 (variant), DLT-10-P18.S1 (marker calls), DLT-18.1, DLT-10, DLT-18.3
  <1>2 [req] On generation exhaustion, finalise by cancellation exactly as TDL-9 specifies, outside the exhausted budget; no unmatched provisional allocation is applied, no foreign register changes and a failed compute does not apply either part.   deps: DLT-10-P37.S1 (TDL-9), DLT-2-P3.S1 (register)
  <1>3 [req] **Leak rule** (successful source generation only, excluding the declared fault/measurement outputs): (`T-LEAK`): for `ctrl` and `adj`, every register allocated during the generation is freed during it; for `compute`, every register allocated during gen(use) is freed during it, while a register allocated during gen(f) and not freed during it is freed by adjoint(E_f), in which its `qalloc` event becomes a `qfree` event, so gen(use) MUST NOT free it (`T-FOREIGN`).   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register)
  <1>4 [req] Outside generations the check is at program end (§6.6): a register that is still live then, neither freed by device code or the host (`bennett_qreg_free`) nor consumed by a `measure`, is `T-LEAK`.   deps: DLT-2-P3.S1 (register), DLT-6.6
  <1>5 [non] *(non-normative)* The classical part of an action region (G) runs once per invocation; its effect on outliving memory is the events of TDL-5, so under `ctrl` it happens exactly on the branch where the control is 1 (the audit's counterexample to 0.1).   deps: DLT-10-P25.S1 (TDL-5), DLT-7.1-P7.S3 (action region)
  <1>6 [req] NS §4.2 requires "allocations inside released clean or borrowed and restored": `T-LEAK` and `T-CLEAN` are those checks.
````

### §18.5 Oracle semantics   [DLT-18.5]

````text
DLT-18.5-P1
  <1>1 [req] An `oracle` event applies, on every basis state of its operands, the permutation |x⟩|t⟩|e⟩ ↦ |x⟩|t ⊕ payload(F_B(x, S))⟩|e ⊕ code(F_B(x, S))⟩ where F_B is the reference interpreter's result on the reference object of the dispatched shape (§16) with the token's budget, and S is the entry state of §8.5 (the caller's classical memory at the call).   deps: DLT-16-P1.S1 (reference object), DLT-16, DLT-8.5
  <1>2 [req] It is an involution (ISA §5.2).   deps: ISA-5.2
````

### §18.6 Reversible semantics   [DLT-18.6]

````text
DLT-18.6-P1
  <1>1 [req] `reversible(f, budget, env)` and the whole-program R mode (§19.2) run f on the R tier (ISA §3.1): its classical effects on memory are those of §18.1, its effects are ISA device models on the tape (§11.2), its region calls are R-tier region calls (§7.5b), and the run history (ISA §7.4) is retained, so the whole run is reversible by `bennett_reverse` (ISA §10).   deps: DLT-19.2, ISA-3.1, DLT-18.1, DLT-11.2, DLT-7.5-P3, ISA-7.4, ISA-10
  <1>2 [req] A fault ends the run (§17.6).   deps: DLT-17.6
````

### §18.7 Conformance   [DLT-18.7]

````text
DLT-18.7-P1
  <1>1 [req] A plugin and an executor (ISA §1.2) together conform iff, for every module the rules accept or block, every host input and every sequence of measurement and `observe` outcomes, outside the executions that reach a blocker point: the probability of that sequence, every classical value the host observes (return values of device entries, memory they write, console output), every fault code and every trap equal those of the reference semantics; and the quantum state at every measurement and at every device-entry return equals the reference state, exactly when the program uses permutation gates only, and otherwise within the error bound its certificate states (ISA §12.3).   deps: DLT-6.5-P10.S1 (blocker point), ISA-1.2, ISA-12.3
  <1>2 [req] A program that reaches `T-CLEAN` in the reference semantics is erroneous; an executor that cannot test cleanliness (hardware) need not reproduce that trap (ISA §17 item 14).   deps: ISA-17-P15
DLT-18.7-P2
  <1>1 [req] **Outcome table** (NS §5.1: "one outcome table governs §3.2, §5.1 and §8"). For every input of a declared domain the comparison with the native comparison build (§17.7) has one of four outcomes:   deps: DLT-3.2, DLT-5.1, DLT-8, DLT-17.7
DLT-18.7-P3
  <1>1 [req] native-comparable success | the reference completes without fault and no layout-dependent value influences the result | the artefact's results equal native
DLT-18.7-P4
  <1>1 [req] reference fault | the reference faults (code ≠ 0) | the artefact reports the same code; native supplies no cause (it may trap, silently read adjacent memory or hang)
DLT-18.7-P5
  <1>1 [req] layout-dependent | the reference interpreter's address provenance shows a host-stack address, or a `blockaddress` value (§14.9), influencing the result | validated against the reference interpreter instead of native, counted separately   deps: DLT-14.9
DLT-18.7-P6
  <1>1 [req] classifier-flagged undefined | an instrumented build (UBSan, ASan, MSan) flags the input (NS §3.2) | excluded from comparison, counted separately
````

### §19.5 Layout: the comparison link   [DLT-19.5]

````text
DLT-19.5-P1
  <1>1 [req] The driver links the materialised module natively (§17.7) with a linker script that fixes the addresses: non-PIE; identical-code folding and constant merging off; the null region [0, `null_size`) with `null_size` = 4096; the data sections (`.rodata`, `.data`, `.bss`, in that order) from `data_base` = 4096; the text from `text_base` = 0x400000, or, when the device ranges below (data, heap, arena, interface regions, computed first) end above 0x400000, from the first multiple of 0x200000 at or after their end, so that the native comparison binary maps its code disjointly from them; the defaults are options (`--bennett-layout-data-base`, `--bennett-layout-text-base`, §24).   deps: DLT-12.1-P1.S6 (materialised module), DLT-17.7-P1.S1 (native comparison binary), DLT-17.7, DLT-24

DLT-19.5-P5
````


````text
DLT-20.4-P1
  <1>1 [req] Poll points at loop back edges and function entries (N35) call `__bennett_rt_poll()`, which checks the timer model (deterministic, driven by the clock model) and the PLIC's pending bits; on delivery it sets the CSRs (`scause`, `sepc`, `stval`, `sstatus`) and calls the trap vector `stvec` by A(F) dispatch (§14.2).   deps: DLT-12.2-P37.S1 (N35), DLT-14.2
  <1>2 [req] Interrupts are therefore taken at poll points only, a deterministic choice recorded in the certificate; NS §3.2's single-thread assumption covers the uniprocessor kernel (`CONFIG_SMP=n`, xv6 `CPUS=1`).
````


### §25.1 Blockers   [DLT-25.1]

````text
DLT-25.1-P1
  <1>1 [req] A **blocker** is a capability the dialect fully specifies whose stated case has no realisation on ISA 0.8.
  <1>2 [req] BLK-3 has been retired by §8.7.   deps: DLT-8.7
  <1>3 [req] Unlike the original outline list, BLK-5 can affect typed fault points in R-tier rungs; successful executions remain covered.   deps: DLT-25.1-P4.S1 (BLK-5)
  <1>4 [req] The maintainer ruled (2026-10-29) that ISA 0.9 waits until this dialect is council-accepted.
DLT-25.1-P2
  <1>1 [def] **BLK-1** = ISA-4 | `BD-B-ISA4` | NS §3.1 handle tables; §4.1, §4.2 dynamic allocation ("real allocation"); Bennett.jl vectors of qubits; adjoints of generations whose register set is known only at run time | allocation sites or entry parameter/result roots whose handles persist across entries without a finite instance bound (§6.5); register widths with value set ⊤ (§3.4); a Co width with an unbounded value set (TDL-10) | direct `qreg` values for handles that stay out of memory; static register files with dispatch for bounded sites (§6.5) | (i) a dynamic-width type `qreg[*]`; `q = qreg.new cls n` with n an `i64` value yields `qreg[*]`; `w = qreg.width q`. (ii) Binding a `qreg[*]` to a `wire[n]` or `region[A,W]` slot checks the width at the call: CC trap, R fault `FAULT_UB_TRAP`, on a mismatch.
````
